head: 8201fa1
note: Read-only hunt over the round-4 tree. Committed BEFORE any fixing so the findings cannot be edited to match what was fixed. Area file lists union to exactly the 76 changed non-docs files (lesson L-048).

findings.title: The BUG-244 recovery does not require a lost response: a verbatim replay of a SUCCESSFUL refresh mints a live child session, unaudited, and kicks the tablet off
findings.requirement: spec P3 / docs/Threat_Model.md T20 — rotation: a consumed child refresh token must not grant again, and a re-presentation is the theft signal (revoke + audit). Also L-040 (a grant is single-use AND time-bounded).
findings.mechanism: The recovery predicate at child-auth.ts:255-259 is `refreshRequestId !== undefined && row.used_request_id === refreshRequestId && row.replaced_by !== null && row.live`, and the only extra condition is that the replacement row is still unused (child-auth.ts:261-264). NOTHING in that set tests the premise the whole design rests on — that the response never reached the device. After a completely ordinary, fully successful refresh, the normal path at child-auth.ts:323-326 stores `used_at`, `replaced_by = next.id` AND `used_request_id = refreshRequestId` on the token it consumed, while the token it issued sits unused in the tablet's storage until the access token expires (childAccessTtlSeconds = 900s in config.ts:215, and indefinitely while the app is closed). For that entire interval the consumed token plus the id — both of which travelled together in the SAME request body — satisfy every branch of the predicate, so re-posting that one captured/logged body returns 200 with a fresh access token and a fresh refresh token (child-auth.ts:286-296), writes NO audit event (only the info log at 281-285), and retires the tablet's unclaimed token (276-279). The tablet's next refresh then presents a token whose `used_request_id` no longer matches the new id it mints, so it falls through to child-auth.ts:299-307: session revoked with reason 'refresh_token_reuse' and the device stamped. The comment at 237-254 asserts a recovery is 'the rightful holder retrying the very refresh that rotated it'; the code cannot tell that from a replay of a refresh that already succeeded, and unlike the 60s grace the lead refused (rejected reason quoted at mobile-r2.review.test.ts:239-242) this relaxation has no time bound at all.
findings.repro: In apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts: `const d = await pairedDevice('Steady state tablet'); const rid = randomUUID(); const ok = await json<{refreshToken:string}>(await refresh(d.refreshToken, rid));` — the response ARRIVED, the tablet holds ok.refreshToken and nothing was lost. Now replay the identical body: `const replay = await refresh(d.refreshToken, rid);` Expected by rotation: `expect(replay.status).toBe(401)` and `expect(await auditActions(d.fam.familyId)).toContain('child_session.revoked_token_reuse')`. Actual: 200, a usable accessToken and refreshToken, no audit row. Then the child's own token is dead: `expect((await refresh(ok.refreshToken, randomUUID())).status).toBe(401)` and `sessionRow(...).revoke_reason === 'refresh_token_reuse'`.
findings.user_impact: Anyone who obtains one child-refresh request body (a TLS-terminating proxy, an edge/WAF body log, a crash reporter or analytics SDK that captures request bodies, a forensic dump of the tablet taken mid-refresh) gets a live, renewable child session — access to that child's homework, practice and profile — with no audit event for the parent or ops to see, where before this diff the same captured body was worthless and self-reported as theft. The child's tablet is then unpaired on its next refresh ('Ask a grown-up to connect this device again') and a parent must mint a new pairing code.
findings.not_a_false_positive: The `recovering` predicate at child-auth.ts:255-259 is the complete guard — there is no freshness check on `used_at`, no single-use marker and no check that the earlier response failed; `used_at` is only read to be copied back at line 277, so it constrains nothing. The closest existing test, 'once the replacement has been used, even the right id is theft' (mobile-r2.review.test.ts:325-334), deliberately consumes the replacement FIRST (line 331) and so only covers the window AFTER the tablet has moved on; no test replays a successful refresh while its replacement is still unclaimed. The other negative cases (313-323, 336-341) all vary the id, which this replay does not. docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-244's 'Residual, deliberate' list covers only (a) a MITM who captured the lost RESPONSE, (b) a device that never retries, (c) two concurrent presentations — not a replay of a refresh that succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: AND the id check with a short freshness bound on the rotation, e.g. `row.used_at > now() - interval '2 minutes'` (a client retry horizon), and treat the recovery as single-use per lineage (a recovery counter, or clear `used_request_id` on the consumed row once the chain has been re-pointed). Adding a bound on top of the id does not reintroduce the refused design — the id still stops a blind replay, while the bound stops a replay of a completed request; the 'second lost response in a row' case (mobile-r2.review.test.ts:302-311) happens within seconds and still passes.

findings.title: The retired replacement inherits used_request_id and replaced_by, so it is a second recovery key — the code's claim that retiring 'kills any copy intercepted from the lost response' is false
findings.requirement: L-040 (a grant is single-use); the explicit claim at child-auth.ts:252-254 and mobile-r2.review.test.ts:296-297 that the replacement carried by the lost response is dead once retired.
findings.mechanism: When a recovery is served, child-auth.ts:276-279 stamps the retired replacement with `used_at = ${row.used_at}`, `replaced_by = ${next.id}` AND `used_request_id = ${refreshRequestId}`. That row now satisfies the recovery predicate at 255-259 in its own right (used_at set, used_request_id === the same id, replaced_by non-null, session live), so presenting the retired replacement WITH that id enters the branch at 260, finds the current head unclaimed, and issues yet another token — exactly what the comment at 252-254 says cannot happen ('retiring it also kills any copy intercepted from the lost response'). The comment at 274-275 ('keeps this token's original used_at, so it never gets a recovery window of its own') is reasoning left over from the withdrawn time-window design: under the id design `used_at`'s value is never compared to anything, so it prevents nothing. Writing the id onto the retired row is also unnecessary for the documented 'second lost response' behaviour, which works through the original row because 280 re-points `row.replaced_by` to the new head.
findings.repro:
`const d = await pairedDevice('Intercepted tablet'); const rid = randomUUID(); const lost = await json<{refreshToken:string}>(await refresh(d.refreshToken, rid)); // response intercepted, never seen by the tablet
expect((await refresh(d.refreshToken, rid)).status).toBe(200); // the tablet recovers; lost.refreshToken is now 'retired'
// The interceptor holds lost.refreshToken and saw rid in the same exchange:
expect((await refresh(lost.refreshToken, rid)).status).toBe(401); // FAILS: 200, a fresh chain, no audit event` — and the tablet's recovered token is retired underneath it, so its next refresh with a new id returns 401 and revokes the session.
findings.user_impact: An attacker who captured one lost refresh response keeps a working credential for the child's session after the tablet has already recovered, instead of holding a dead token — and their use of it is silent (no `child_session.revoked_token_reuse` audit row), while the child's tablet is the one that ends up unpaired. It also makes docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-244's stated residual ('the id gives such an attacker nothing new') untrue, so the risk the lead signed off on is not the risk that shipped.
findings.not_a_false_positive: The recovery predicate does not distinguish an originally-consumed row from a retired replacement — there is no terminal marker, and the `used_at` value it preserves is never read as a bound. The test at mobile-r2.review.test.ts:296-299 presents exactly this token but with `randomUUID()` (a fresh id), which is why it sees 401; with `rid` it would see 200. No other test presents a retired replacement.
findings.suggested_fix: When retiring the replacement at child-auth.ts:276-279, do not copy the request id onto it — set `used_request_id = null` (or a terminal marker) so only the row that the id originally consumed can ever be recovered; the 'twice lost' case still works because line 280 re-points the original row to the new head. Then fix the comments at 252-254, 274-275 and mobile-r2.review.test.ts:296-297 to say what the code does.

findings.title: New HUNT4-MOB-4 test pins a fixture to the frozen test clock but the code compares with the database clock: it goes red on 2026-10-01 (L-027)
findings.requirement: L-027 — a fixture pinned to a clock must not depend on when the suite runs.
findings.mechanism: The test inserts the second session with `created_at = FIXED_NOW` and `expires_at = FIXED_NOW + 7 days` (mobile-r2.review.test.ts:379-380), where FIXED_NOW is the hard-coded `2026-09-24T15:00:00Z` of line 18. The property under test is the `not exists (... s.revoked_at is null and s.expires_at > now())` guard in stampDeviceWhenNoLiveSession (child-auth.ts:57-60), which uses the DATABASE clock. Nothing pins the database clock: harness.ts:120-121 only sets `pencillift.request_now`, and migration 0780 uses that setting solely inside `app.request_instant()` (0780_request_instant.sql:16-21) — `now()` is untouched, and the shim defines no now() override. So from 2026-10-01T15:00:00Z the inserted session is no longer live, the device IS stamped, and the final assertion `expect((await devices(...))[0]!.revokedAt).toBeNull()` fails permanently. Today is 2026-09-26, so the suite has five days left. The pre-existing twin at lines 182-185 has the same construction and fails at the same instant.
findings.repro: Run `pnpm --filter @pencillift/api run test -- mobile-r2.review` with the machine clock at 2026-10-02: 'a device that still has a live session stays connected' fails on the last assertion (revokedAt is a timestamp, not null). Equivalently, replace 7 days with `-1` days today and watch it fail for the same reason.
findings.user_impact: CI goes red on a date with no code change behind it; the pressure is then to weaken or delete the assertion that protects the shared-device guard, which is how a real regression in stampDeviceWhenNoLiveSession would get through unnoticed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a database clock override: supabase/tests/harness.ts sets only `pencillift.request_now`; grep over supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql finds no `now()` function definition; migration 0780 wires the setting into `app.request_instant()` only, and the guard at child-auth.ts:59 calls `now()` directly. The other FIXED_NOW use in this file (line 105) compares against a value derived from `deps.clock()`, so it is stable; these two inserts are not.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the second session with database-relative timestamps (`now()`, `now() + interval '7 days'`) or stamp it through the pinned request instant the code actually compares against, and fix the pre-existing twin at lines 182-185 in the same pass.

findings.title: The HUNT4-MOB-1 docstring in the same commit says the finding is OPEN and 'nothing about the reuse gate was changed', which the commit's own recovery branch contradicts
findings.requirement: A comment must not state something the code does not do (records: docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-244 is recorded 'closed' by this very change).
findings.mechanism: The block added at mobile-r2.review.test.ts:232-268 states 'HUNT4-MOB-1 — OPEN, not fixed here', 'Weakening either is a lead decision, so reuse stays immediate revocation' (245) and 'no failing-test-first for HUNT4-MOB-1 exists, because nothing about the reuse gate was changed' (248-249), and its describe title still reads '(HUNT4-MOB-1 open)' (255). The same commit adds the recovery branch at child-auth.ts:255-298, which is precisely a change to the reuse gate, and docs/Bug_Ledger.md:251 records BUG-244 (= HUNT4-MOB-1) as closed by it. The two blocks in this one file therefore tell a reader opposite things about whether a rotated token can ever be served.
findings.repro: Read mobile-r2.review.test.ts top to bottom: lines 232-254 assert the reuse gate is unconditional immediate revocation; lines 270-342 document and exercise the recovery that serves a rotated token. Both describe the same endpoint at the same commit.
findings.user_impact: A later reviewer or fixer who trusts lines 232-254 will believe /v1/child/refresh cannot serve a used token and will not examine the recovery branch at all — which is how HUNT5-A-1 and HUNT5-A-2 stay unfound. It also leaves the repo's own narrative of what was decided unreliable.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I verified the diff added both blocks in the same commit (both appear as added lines in `git diff 8bc022b 8201fa1` for this file) and that the reuse gate genuinely changed (child-auth.ts:236-298 is new). docs/Bug_Ledger.md:251 records BUG-244 as 'closed ... designed and fixed by the lead in the round after it (migration 0880)', so the 'OPEN / unchanged' wording is stale, not an accepted deferral.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring to say what is now true: reuse is immediate revocation EXCEPT for the id-carrying recovery, and this case pins the no-id replay path (which is why it still 401s). Retitle the describe without '(HUNT4-MOB-1 open)' and drop the obsolete 'if the lead accepts a bounded grace' instructions.

findings.title: The 'second session on a shared tablet' justification describes a state no API path can produce, and the new test creates it with raw SQL
findings.requirement: A comment must not claim behaviour the code cannot reach; a test must not prove a property through a state the user's own path cannot create.
findings.mechanism: The docstring added at child-auth.ts:44-51 justifies the `not exists` guard with 'so a second session on a shared tablet keeps it connected'. Two live sessions on one `child_devices` row cannot exist in production: the only production insert of `public.child_sessions` is /pair (child-auth.ts:146-151), and it always inserts a BRAND NEW `child_devices` row first (142-145) — which the same test file states at line 158 ('every re-pair added another connected row for the same tablet'). The new test at mobile-r2.review.test.ts:374-384 manufactures the state with `api.db.sql` INSERT, so what it verifies is only reachable by raw SQL. The guard itself is still load-bearing for a different case (a `!row.live` refresh where liveness failed for a reason other than the session ending — archived child, deleted family, revoked device — where the session is still live and must not stamp the device), so this is about the stated justification and the test's scenario, not the guard.
findings.repro: Grep the tree for `insert into public.child_sessions`: only child-auth.ts:147 (production, always paired with a fresh child_devices insert at 142) and test/fixture files. Pair the same physical tablet twice through /v1/child/pair and query `select device_id, count(*) from public.child_sessions group by 1` — every count is 1, and GET /v1/devices lists two rows for the one tablet.
findings.user_impact: A parent who re-pairs a tablet sees two 'Connected' rows for one device, not one row with two sessions; a reader of this comment will believe the opposite and may 'fix' the duplicate-row artifact by reusing device rows, which would then make the reuse-revocation stamp stop firing (one device row with a live session from the re-pair keeps the tablet listed as Connected after a theft revocation).
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked every insert site for public.child_sessions (child-auth.ts:147 only, in production) and confirmed /pair inserts a new child_devices row per redemption with no lookup of an existing row by label or platform (child-auth.ts:142-145). The claim at mobile-r2.review.test.ts:158 in the same file contradicts the one at child-auth.ts:49, so one of them is wrong, and the code says which.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to the case the guard really serves — a refresh whose liveness failed for a reason other than the session ending (archived child, deleted family, revoked device) must not stamp a device whose session is still live — and label the raw-SQL test as a unit test of that guard rather than as a re-pair scenario.

sweeps_sound: A replay with no id, or with a different id, still revokes the session and audits it: the guard at apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:256-257 short-circuits on `refreshRequestId !== undefined` and compares with `row.used_request_id`, which is null for tokens rotated by an id-less client (line 325), so null === uuid is false and both cases fall through to the revoke at 299.

The recovery cannot resurrect a dead session or bypass consent: `row.live` at child-auth.ts:259 carries the whole liveness expression selected at 217-218 (token expiry, session revoked/expired, device revoked, child active, family not deleted), and consent is re-checked at 266 before any token is issued — same gate and same order as the normal path at 309-315.

The chain cannot fork: each recovery retires the current head under `for update` (child-auth.ts:261-264) and re-points the presented row to the new head (280), so at most one unclaimed token per session exists; a second concurrent recovery re-reads the head as used and falls through to revocation, which is the concurrency case docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-244 records as deliberate.
The endpoint is not an existence oracle: 'reused' and 'invalid' both produce the same 401 and the same message at child-auth.ts:339-340, so a replayer cannot tell a known token from an unknown one.
The new log line carries no child identity or homework: child-auth.ts:281-285 emits only `event` and `code`, within the payload-free LogEvent contract at apps/api/src/middleware/context.ts:20-30.

A device whose refresh token failed liveness for a reason other than the session ending is not stamped: the `not exists` clause at child-auth.ts:57-60 keeps a live session's device connected, so the `!row.live` branch at 309-313 cannot be used by an attacker holding an old token to disconnect a working tablet.

Every other path that ends a child session already stamps public.child_devices, so the test's claim at apps/api/tests/mobile-r2.review.test.ts:349 that only reuse-revocation and expiry were left is true: guardians.ts:725, family.ts:523 and 578, and migrations 0620:104, 0680:36, 0710:265/365, 0840:112/185. /consent/start cannot create a consent-blocked-but-live-session state either, since it refuses when the latest record is verified (guardians.ts:638-642).

Lock ordering in both new write paths is token → session → device (child-auth.ts:225, 299, 306), the same order as the pre-existing logout path (349-351), so two concurrent revocations cannot deadlock (BUG-106).
L-006 holds: the diff writes only scalar parameters (child-auth.ts:276-280, 323-326) and adds no bare `::jsonb` cast anywhere.

Migration 0880 is additive and idempotent (`add column if not exists`, `create index if not exists`), adds no public table so the schema_invariants RLS rule does not apply, and grants nothing to anon/authenticated/pl_child — pinned by supabase/tests/hardening_r1_db2.test.ts:541-547; the column is nullable as the id-less path at child-auth.ts:325 requires.

The new self-referencing `replaced_by` chain cannot leave a dangling FK for the pruner: app.prune_session_rows deletes all of a session's tokens as one set (supabase/migrations/0850_hardening_r1_db2.sql:134-137) before deleting the session, so no surviving row can reference a deleted one.

The contract change is backward compatible: `refreshRequestId` is optional (packages/contracts/src/auth.ts:67) inside a strictObject, so an installed app that omits it parses and takes the pre-diff path exactly, and no other client posts to /v1/child/refresh (only apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:196, the single token source per L-007).
A-child-auth.notes: Read-only throughout: no files written, no git state changed, no test run (a Postgres-backed run would write into test-results/, so HUNT5-A-1/A-2/A-3 are established by reading the code and the harness rather than by executing a failing case). Three things I could not check from my files: (1) the mobile side of BUG-244 belongs to another reviewer, but note that apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:177-180 swallows a failed `deleteItem` of the stored request id while clearing the in-memory copy first, which would make one id persist across many refreshes and widen HUNT5-A-1's replay surface to every past request body — worth handing to whoever owns that file. (2) GET /v1/devices and apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts render the 'Connected' state the HUNT4-MOB-4 stamp feeds; I read the route (family.ts:536-566) but not the mobile view. (3) A non-finding landmine for the lead: this test file now performs 16 pairing redemptions against one rate-limit bucket of 20 per 15 minutes (RATE_RULES.pairingRedeemPerNetwork) under a frozen clock that never advances the window, so the next four `pairedDevice(...)` calls added to it will start failing at the `expect(paired.status).toBe(201)` in the helper. Also outside the diff and not filed: a child session is never extended on refresh (child-auth.ts:146-151 sets expires_at once at pair time), so every paired device stops working 30 days after pairing and needs a new pairing code — if that is not the intended product behaviour it is a separate, pre-existing issue.

findings.title: The archive route can never reach the slot-reconciliation the same commit's comment and test claim it performs
findings.requirement: FL-R4-01 / MOB-R4-LOCK-06 (the archive route is the parent-visible remedy for a stranded paid slot)
findings.mechanism: family.ts:510-511 now refuses any child with an open deletion request (visibleChild, whose predicate at family.ts:110-114 excludes `status in ('requested','processing')`) with a 404 BEFORE the release statement at family.ts:516-517 ever runs. The comment immediately above that statement (family.ts:512-515) justifies moving the release outside the `status !== 'archived'` guard because "it also reconciles an already-archived child that still holds an open assignment — the state a deletion request used to leave behind, and the state a crash between these statements can leave". Neither named state is reachable: (a) the deletion-pending state is exactly what the new visibleChild gate 404s two lines earlier, and (b) the 'crash between these statements' state cannot exist because all of the statements run inside one `deps.db.asService` transaction (family.ts:505-530), so a crash rolls them back together. `status='archived'` is only ever written by this route (family.ts:519) and by request_deletion (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:128), and billing's `releaseSlotlessProfiles` only touches `status='active'` rows (services/billing-sync.ts:975-981), so the only production producer of 'archived + open slot' is the deletion path the gate now rejects. The FL-R4-01 regression test (apps/api/tests/family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:92-105) 'proves' the remedy with a hand-seeded archived child that has NO deletion_requests row — a fixture that bypasses the very state its own comment (lines 93-94: 'a purge that dead-letters') names.
findings.repro: In apps/api/tests: seed a family with paidSlots 2, an archived child C with an open row in public.child_slot_assignments, and an open child-scope row in public.deletion_requests for C (status 'requested') — i.e. the state request_deletion produces when its release does not run (see HUNT5-B-2). POST /v1/children/C/archive with an unlocked parent token. Expected by the comment: 200 and the slot released. Actual: 404 'Child not found' and `select count(*) from public.child_slot_assignments where child_id = C and released_at is null` is still 1. Then show no other route frees it: POST /v1/children/C/activate -> 404, PATCH /v1/children/C -> 422 CHILD_DELETION_PENDING, POST /v1/deletion {scope:'child',childId:C} -> 409 CONFLICT (deletion_requests_one_open, migrations/0620:74).
findings.user_impact: If a paid slot is ever left assigned to a child whose deletion is under way (a purge that exhausts its retries, or a request filed by any path that does not go through this API handler), the family has no way to get it back: every child route answers 404/422 and re-requesting the deletion is a conflict. Activating a sibling answers 'All 1 paid child slots are in use. Add a child slot to your plan first.' — the parent is told to buy capacity they already pay for. The comment tells the next maintainer a remedy exists, so nobody will look for one.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the guard that would prevent this and it is the cause, not the cure: visibleChild at family.ts:104-115 returns undefined for `d.status in ('requested','processing')` and family.ts:511 throws NOT_FOUND before line 516. The companion test apps/api/tests/family-profile.review.test.ts:208-214 ('refuses archiving while the deletion is open') asserts exactly this 404, so the two tests in the same commit assert contradictory capabilities. No Bug_Ledger entry records this as a deferral: BUG-230 covers FL-R4-03/04 only, and the FL-R4-01 write-up in apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts:494-503 still asserts the archive route as the fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one and make the code and the prose agree. Either (a) keep the MOB-R4-LOCK-06 404 and delete the 'a deletion request used to leave behind / a crash between these statements' sentences plus the second FL-R4-01 test, replacing them with an honest note that a stranded slot is now a support/ops fix (and say so in the Bug_Ledger); or (b) keep the reconciliation and let the archive route run the release for a deletion-pending child before refusing the archive itself (release first, then throw the 404/422), which preserves MOB-R4-LOCK-06's client agreement while keeping a parent-visible remedy. Either way the archive route's unconditional release currently writes a capacity change with no audit_events row (family.ts:516-517 sits outside the `child.archived` audit at 525-527) — add one if it stays.

findings.title: FL-R4-01's slot release lives in the API handler, not in request_deletion, which `authenticated` may call directly
findings.requirement: L-037 (the same pre-check must hold on EVERY surface that offers the action); FL-R4-01
findings.mechanism: The release is a separate statement in the Hono handler: privacy.ts:563 calls releaseChildSlot (privacy.ts:520-533) after the RPC. `public.request_deletion` itself never touches public.child_slot_assignments (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:80-141) and is granted to the client role: `grant execute on function public.request_deletion(uuid, uuid) to authenticated, service_role` (0840:144). Its own gates are satisfiable outside the API — app.is_family_member plus app.has_recent_adult_unlock(), which keys on (app.current_user_id(), jwt 'session_id') (0001_core_identity.sql:255-262) — so a parent's Supabase access token calling POST /rest/v1/rpc/request_deletion archives the child, revokes its sessions and enqueues the purge while the paid slot stays assigned. docs/Architecture.md:79-82 treats the Data API as a live client surface and states the design rule that client-reachable writes are backstopped in the database (BUG-240 is the same class of finding). The lead's own justification at privacy.ts:506-509 is atomicity — 'so a rollback cannot leave the slot released without the request' — which holds only for the one caller that runs the extra statement.
findings.repro: In a db authorization test (supabase/tests): as `authenticated` with the owner's claims and a live row in private.adult_unlocks, `select * from public.request_deletion(:family, :child)` directly. Assert the child is archived and then `select count(*) from public.child_slot_assignments where child_id = :child and released_at is null` — it is still 1 (the API route's own test, apps/api/tests/family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:62-90, gets 0 because it goes through POST /v1/deletion). Then, via the API, POST /v1/children/<sibling>/activate -> 422 NEEDS_PAID_SLOT although paid_slots is 1 and the only holder is a child being deleted.
findings.user_impact: A family whose deletion request reached the database by any route other than this one handler keeps paying for a slot held by a child whose data is being erased, is told to buy another slot to start a sibling, and — because of HUNT5-B-1 — has no way to free it. If the purge job dead-letters, the slot is consumed indefinitely.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a database-side backstop and there is none: no trigger or statement in any migration releases child_slot_assignments at request time (grep of `child_slot_assignments` across supabase/migrations gives only the table/trigger in 0200_billing.sql and the three purge deletes in 0620:214, 0710:502, 0820:120, which run at purge, not at request). Migration 0860's re-activation trigger is a backstop for activation only, not for capacity. The route's own 23505 branch (privacy.ts:571-573) means a second POST /v1/deletion cannot repair the missed release either.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the release into `public.request_deletion` itself (a new migration that adds `update public.child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'archived' where family_id = p_family and child_id = p_child and released_at is null` in the `else` branch beside the child archive at 0840:128), keeping the API statement only as an idempotent belt-and-braces or dropping it. That also removes the `set local role service_role` / `set local role authenticated` pair, whose only plausible failure mode (SQLSTATE 42501) is caught by privacy.ts:576-586 and reported to the parent as 'Enter your parent PIN to continue' — a message that can never be satisfied.

findings.title: The unresolved CHILD-report branch is bounded newest-first, so a child's oldest open report is hidden — the failure CS-R2-07 removed
findings.requirement: CS-R2-07 / CS-R4-01 (no unresolved report a grown-up must act on is hidden from the family's list)
findings.mechanism: The child branch is `order by created_at desc limit 200` (privacy.ts:832-835), while the system branch next to it is `order by created_at asc` (privacy.ts:831) precisely because — in the file's own words at privacy.ts:132-136 and 816-818 — 'a newest-first cap made an old open flag unreachable for good once newer reports filled the page, while an oldest-first bound drains'. The documented reason for newest-first is stated only for the parent branch ('nothing the family does drains that branch; the newest is what a guardian needs to see', privacy.ts:140-142); the sentence about the child branch justifies only that it is a SEPARATE branch, not its direction. A child's report IS actionable (PATCH /safety-reports/:id accepts reporter_kind 'child', privacy.ts:891-895), so by the file's own rule it belongs on the oldest-first side. Nothing auto-resolves a child report (REPORT_TRANSITIONS at privacy.ts:88-93 leaves 'open' until a grown-up acts) and the child may file 20/hour (RULES.childReportPerChild, privacy.ts:63), so open child reports accumulate monotonically; past 200 the earliest ones — the most likely genuine disclosure, and the one a guardian most needs — are absent from the response and from every surface that reads it.
findings.repro: Extend apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts: seed one family, insert one child report at T0 ('upsetting'), then UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE + 5 further child reports at T0 + n minutes (timestamps derived from the first row, L-027). GET /v1/safety-reports as an unlocked guardian and assert `reports.map(r => r.id)` contains the T0 id — it does not. Mirror of the existing CS-R4-01 case at privacy-r2.review.test.ts:661-703, which only covers parent-filed fillers.
findings.user_impact: A child who uses the 'Get help' button regularly (and guardians who leave reports open, which the product never closes for them) pushes the child's own earliest report out of the parent's list. The guardian sees no trace of it and no count telling them anything is missing, so the first and usually most serious thing the child said is the thing they cannot read or act on.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the two things that could prevent it. (1) It is not caught by the existing CS-R4-01 test: that test's fillers are all `reporter_kind = 'parent'` (privacy-r2.review.test.ts:669-676) and it asserts the child report is listed only because there is exactly one of them. (2) It is not prevented by a second read path: there is no GET /v1/safety-reports/:id — the routes are POST /safety-reports, GET /safety-reports and PATCH /safety-reports/:id — so this list is the family's only way to discover a report id. The bound does drain (resolving newer rows eventually surfaces the oldest), so this is 'hidden until 200 newer are resolved', not 'unreachable for good'; that is still the outcome CS-R2-07 was filed about.
findings.suggested_fix: Order the child branch `created_at asc` like the system branch, since both kinds are actionable by the guardian and the oldest is the one that must not be hidden; keep newest-first only for the parent branch, which the family cannot drain. Update the rationale at privacy.ts:137-144 accordingly. If both ends matter, the honest fix is BUG-117's keyset paging plus an unresolved count per kind, which privacy.ts:819-821 currently declares unnecessary.

findings.title: With 200 open system flags the newest flag is absent from the page the flag email tells the parent to open
findings.requirement: CS-R4-01 (a flag the family is emailed about is reachable on the surface the email names)
findings.mechanism: The system branch takes the 200 OLDEST unresolved flags (privacy.ts:828-831). Once 200 are open, a flag filed now is row 201 and is not in the response at all. Meanwhile every flag triggers an email whose body says 'Please sign in to the PencilLift parent portal and open Privacy & safety to see the flag and what you can do next: <origin>/app/privacy' (apps/api/src/providers/index.ts:139-148, portalUrl built at apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:402). That page renders exactly this list, and there is no GET /v1/safety-reports/:id and no per-report deep link, so the flag the email announces cannot be found or acted on until the family clears 200 older ones. The comment at privacy.ts:819-821 dismisses keyset paging on the grounds that 'nothing unresolved can become permanently unreachable' — true, but the email makes a stronger promise than eventual reachability.
findings.repro: In apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts: build a flagged family, then insert UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE system rows with created_at earlier than the real flag (shape them to satisfy safety_reports_system_shape: child_id, question_id, note null, status 'escalated', transcription_at, screen_version, screen_categories). GET /v1/safety-reports and assert the real flag's id is in `reports` — it is not, although its parent_email_status is 'sent'.
findings.user_impact: A guardian gets an email saying a recent answer was flagged and to open Privacy & safety to see it; the flag is not on that page, and nothing on the page says anything is missing. The one flag they were told about is the one they cannot see.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that the email is not deep-linked (dispatcher.ts:402 builds only `${origin}/app/privacy`) and that no other family-facing route returns a single report by id (the route table in privacy.ts registers POST /safety-reports, GET /safety-reports, PATCH /safety-reports/:id and the admin pair only). The per-kind split introduced by CS-R4-01 does not help here, because the crowding rows are system flags on the system branch. 200 open flags is the reachable-but-unlikely end of this: it needs a family that accumulates that many severe-risk screens (open-response hyperbole false matches, e.g. the FALSE_MATCH fixture at privacy-r2.review.test.ts:89-96) without a guardian ever clearing one.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the email a per-report destination (or make the list surface an 'N more unresolved' affordance), or return the newest unresolved flags alongside the oldest on the system branch (e.g. 100 oldest UNION 100 newest) so a just-emailed flag is always in the response. At minimum, correct privacy.ts:819-821 so it no longer claims paging is unnecessary.

findings.title: The CS-R4-02 hotline sweep still searches two UUID columns, so the flake its comment says was removed remains
findings.requirement: CS-R4-02 (the safety notice's wording never leaves PencilLift in the family_data export)
findings.mechanism: privacy-r2.review.test.ts:806 strips only `id` and `created_at` before the regex at 807 (`expect(JSON.stringify(withoutIds)).not.toMatch(/988|422-4453/)`), and the comment at 802-805 states 'The identifiers and the instant are dropped before the hotline check ... which reddened this run about once in fifty while nothing had leaked'. But the exported row has five columns, not three: apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts:521-524 selects `id, question_id, child_id, kind, body, safety_template_version, created_at`, so `rest` still contains `question_id` and `child_id`, both random v4 UUIDs. The local TypeScript annotation at privacy-r2.review.test.ts:789-797 omits those two fields, so nothing at compile time reveals that the destructure misses them. '988' can occur inside a hex UUID (about 22 three-character windows per UUID, 1/4096 each), so with two UUIDs per safety row the spurious-failure rate is roughly 1%, i.e. the same order as the 1-in-50 the comment claims to have fixed.
findings.repro: Deterministic version: in the same test, after parsing the export, assert `Object.keys(withoutIds[0]!)` contains neither 'question_id' nor 'child_id' — it contains both. Non-deterministic version: seed the flagged family with a child_profiles id or extracted_questions id containing '988' (e.g. insert with an explicit uuid '98800000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000') and run the test: it fails on line 807 with nothing leaked.
findings.user_impact: None for a family. For the team: a child-safety privacy assertion reddens roughly one run in a hundred with nothing wrong, which is exactly the pressure that gets such an assertion weakened or deleted — and the comment tells the next reader the flake was already dealt with, so they will look elsewhere.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the assertions that would make this moot and they are separate, not substitutes: line 785 (`expect(body).not.toContain(notice!.body)`) and the phrase loop at 780-783 are the load-bearing checks and are flake-free (I verified 'call or text 988' and '1-800-422-4453' are literal substrings of the real templates, packages/domain/src/safety/templates.ts:66-77, so the loop is not a vacuous assertion). Line 807 is the extra 'scoped' sweep, and it is the one that carries the residual flake.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip every identifier the row actually has, or invert the check: `const { kind, body, safety_template_version } = row` and assert on those three fields only — the only ones that could carry wording — rather than on the rest-spread. Then make the comment say what is dropped.

findings.title: GET /v1/family's comment still justifies listing a deletion-pending child by a cancellation the product does not offer
findings.requirement: honesty of in-code rationale (BUG-221 removed the same claim from the user-facing copy)
findings.mechanism: The rationale for keeping a deletion-pending child in GET /v1/family (family.ts:200-210, rewritten in this diff) still reads '… could no longer tell which child a still-cancellable request covered.' No cancellation exists: privacy.ts registers only POST /deletion and GET /deletion, nothing anywhere sets deletion_requests.status = 'cancelled' (grep over apps/api/src and supabase/migrations finds the value only in the CHECK constraint at 0600_operations.sql:17 and in deletionStatusSchema at packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:46), and BUG-221 closed precisely this claim in the portal copy — apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:304-313 now says 'Deletion can't be undone from the app'. The comment survived the rewrite in the same commit that rewrote the lines around it.
findings.repro: Not a runtime defect. Verifiable statically: `grep -rn "cancelled" apps/api/src supabase/migrations | grep deletion_requests` returns only the constraint, while apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:204 and apps/mobile/src/family/children-screen.test.ts:67 still assert the request 'is still cancellable'.
findings.user_impact: None directly. It is the stale half of a defect the team already paid for once (BUG-221): the next person to write parent-facing copy from this rationale will re-introduce 'cancel the request', which is what BUG-221 had to remove.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a cancel path on every surface before filing: no route in apps/api/src/routes (privacy.ts, account.ts, family.ts), no RPC in any migration, and the web notice explicitly denies it. BUG-221 in docs/Bug_Ledger.md:228 records the fix as a copy change only, so the comment is stale rather than a documented deferral.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'a still-cancellable request' with the true reason the row must stay listed — the privacy screens resolve a nickname from this list for the pending-deletion notice, that child's export rows and any safety report about it — and drop the cancellation clause here and in apps/mobile/src/family/children-screen.test.ts:67.

sweeps_sound: The four child routes really do share one deletion predicate: visibleChild (family.ts:110-114), childForEdit (family.ts:139-143) and GET /v1/family (family.ts:210-214) are byte-equivalent on `(d.scope = 'family' or d.target_child_id = c.id) and d.status in ('requested','processing')`, so no route can disagree about which children a pending deletion covers.

The new 422 ordering in PATCH /children/:childId is right, not inverted: request_deletion archives the child in the same transaction that files the request (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:128), so both conditions are true and the deletion check at family.ts:349 must precede the archived check at family.ts:355.

No RLS-dependent bypass in the pairing route's asParent visibility check (family.ts:400): policy deletion_requests_member_read (supabase/migrations/0600_operations.sql:292) is `app.is_family_member(family_id) or app.is_owner_admin()`, so guardian B sees a request guardian A filed — the check is not scoped to requested_by.

The FOR NO KEY UPDATE reasoning in lockFamily (family.ts:60-77) is correct on Postgres's row-lock conflict table: it conflicts with the other writes' FOR UPDATE (so they serialise and the BUG-106 ABBA cycle is gone) and does not conflict with the FOR KEY SHARE an FK insert takes, so the child redeem path is not blocked in turn.

The slot-release UPDATEs add no out-of-order family lock: both set released_at to a non-null value, so app.enforce_slot_capacity returns at supabase/migrations/0200_billing.sql:118-119 before reaching its `perform 1 from public.families ... for update` at line 122.

Freeing the slot at deletion-request time cannot flip the child back to draft: releaseSlotlessProfiles only updates rows with `status = 'active'` whose latest release_reason is 'expired' or 'downgrade' (apps/api/src/services/billing-sync.ts:975-981), and a deletion-pending child is 'archived' with reason 'archived'.

The exported safety_template_version leaks no screen category: a safety row's guard_version is the constant SAFETY_TEMPLATES_VERSION = 'safety-templates.v5' (packages/domain/src/safety/templates.ts:31), written unconditionally at apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:2233 and copied verbatim by keepSafetyNotice at 2188-2190 — it is not a per-category or per-message value.

Nulling the safety body in the export contradicts no other surface: the only reader of child_feedback.body outside export-build is the CHILD route GET /v1/child/assignments/:id under requireChild (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1462), and no parent route selects that column, so the family never saw the wording elsewhere.

No safety wording escapes under another `kind`: the only non-safety body written is TEMPLATE_FALLBACK, generic coaching copy (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:1934), so the `kind = 'safety'` filter at export-build.ts:522 covers every row that can carry the notice.

CONSENT_WITHDRAWN_SCAN_COPY's 'pages were given back to your monthly allowance' is true: settleScansAfterConsentWithdrawal releases the still-'reserved' scan-usage row (apps/api/src/routes/guardians.ts:115-119), and the reservation is only committed at the very end of a successful run (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:1257 and 1263), so an in-flight scan's reservation is always still 'reserved' when the withdrawal settles it.

The three unresolved CTEs cannot duplicate or silently drop a row: they partition on system / child / not-in(system,child) (privacy.ts:830, 834, 841) and reporter_kind is NOT NULL with a three-value CHECK (supabase/migrations/0600_operations.sql:181, 0760_safety_screening.sql:25-26), so the catch-all branch cannot be defeated by a NULL.

The FL-R4-03 rate-limit test can genuinely go red: without the limiter the 31st call (the child PATCH) would return 200 and insert one `child.profile_updated` row, so `expect(audits!.n).toBe(0)` at apps/api/tests/family-hardening-r4.review.test.ts:231 fails, and the 30 successes are pinned exactly (line 219).

The CS-R4-01 test genuinely failed before its fix: every filler row is created_at earlier than the flag (apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts:669-676), so the old single oldest-end page of 200 excluded both the flag and the child report that lines 693-695 now require, and the drain is proved through PATCH /v1/safety-reports/:id rather than raw SQL (lines 705-712).

L-006 holds throughout the diff: every JSON literal reaching Postgres uses `::text::jsonb` (family.ts:373, privacy.ts:455, 597) or tx.json (privacy.ts:447); there is no bare `::jsonb` cast on a parameter.

The archive route stays idempotent after the release moved outside the status guard: the statement is scoped `and released_at is null` (family.ts:517) and app.prevent_mutation is not attached to child_slot_assignments, so a second POST changes nothing.

The service-role switch inside the parent transaction is balanced and correctly scoped: `set local role service_role` / `set local role authenticated` (privacy.ts:521, 531) bracket one statement, SET LOCAL is checked against session_user (the login role is a member of all three per docs/Architecture.md and apps/api/src/db.ts:8-9), the request.jwt.claims GUC set at db.ts:52 survives the switch, and nothing else runs in that transaction after privacy.ts:563.
B-family-privacy-api.notes:
Could not run the test suites: apps/api tests need a live PG16 (`pnpm db:local`) which is not provisioned in this container, and I was read-only, so every claim about test behaviour above is from reading the fixtures, the SQL they exercise and the constraints in supabase/migrations, not from a run. HUNT5-B-6's flake rate is an arithmetic estimate (22 three-char windows per hex UUID, two UUIDs per safety row), not a measurement.

Two things I judged not to be findings but flag for the lead. (1) The 42501 trap noted in HUNT5-B-2's fix: releaseChildSlot's two `set local role` statements and its UPDATE all sit inside the try block at privacy.ts:558-566, whose catch maps SQLSTATE 42501 to 'Enter your parent PIN to continue' (privacy.ts:580-586). In the documented deployment neither can raise 42501 (the login role is a member of service_role, and supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:107 plus hosted defaults give service_role UPDATE on public tables), so I could not make it reachable — but if it ever is, the parent is asked for a PIN forever and their child's data is never deleted. (2) CONSENT_WITHDRAWN_SCAN_COPY's doc comment says it lives in the contracts 'so the portal and the app say the same thing', and only the portal consumes it (apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:139); the mobile child screen deliberately shows no error code (apps/mobile/src/homework/result-view.ts:146-152) and mobile has no parent scan list, so I read that as placement rationale rather than an untrue claim.

Not checked, outside my files: whether the Supabase Data API is actually enabled on the hosted project (HUNT5-B-2's reachability rests on docs/Architecture.md:79-82 treating it as a live surface and on BUG-240 being filed for the same class); the mobile children screen's own deletion-pending behaviour, which is asserted only by source-text regexes (apps/mobile/src/family/children-screen.test.ts:72-79) — that pattern is a test-strength concern in someone else's area; and whether the family_data export's inclusion of q.student_answer_text (export-build.ts:499-509, added by CS-R2-05) weakens CS-R4-02's premise, since the parent can already read the child's answers in the portal's review flow."

findings.title: R4-JOBS-1's truncation retry is still unreachable for 7–10 page scans, and both new tests prove it only at a zero-image input extraction never sends
findings.requirement: JOBS-R2-02 / R4-JOBS-1 (BUG-235): an answer cut off at max_output_tokens gets exactly one retry at a raised output budget whenever the stage cost cap has room for a bigger answer
findings.mechanism: packages/ai/src/run.ts:79-110 `raisedOutputBudget` binary-searches (maxOutputTokens, 2x maxOutputTokens] for a budget `canAttempt` still admits. With terra at 2 micros/input-token and 12/output-token, extraction's cap 150,000 and maxOutputTokens 4,000, the first cut-off attempt is metered at the bound it was admitted with (2E + 48,000, run.ts:196-217), so a raise to x >= 4,001 exists only while (2E+48,000) + (2E+12x) <= 150,000, i.e. E <= 13,497 input tokens. apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:1314-1320 always sends `dataEnvelope(...)` PLUS one `input_image` part per page (and scan-process.ts:1294 throws NO_PAGES for zero pages), and apps/api/src/jobs/spend-ceiling.ts:300-301 charges IMAGE_INPUT_TOKEN_BOUND (1,500) + PART_OVERHEAD_TOKENS (16) per image. I measured the production functions (inputTokenUpperBound + estimateUpperBoundCostMicros + canAttempt, read-only probe): 1 page E=4,541 -> raise 6,986; 6 pages E=12,131 -> raise 4,456; 7 pages E=13,649 -> raise NULL; 10 pages E=18,204 -> raise NULL. packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:31 sets maxPages = 10, so a 7-, 8-, 9- or 10-page scan is inside the product's own limit and still gets NO retry — the exact defect R4-JOBS-1 says it fixed. The first attempt is still admitted at those sizes (estimate 75,298–84,408 < 150,000), so the scan runs, is cut off, and scan-process.ts:1228-1234 turns OUTPUT_TRUNCATED into PermanentFailure SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS -> failed_final. The two new tests cannot see this: apps/api/tests/jobs-r2.review.test.ts:414 builds `input = [{type:'input_text', text:'{}'}]` and feeds it to `inputTokenUpperBound` at :415, i.e. an extraction request with no page image, which the code above makes impossible; their own doc comment at :408-411 admits 'Every real request is larger, and a larger request only leaves the cost cap less headroom', yet the tests are named 'is admitted for extraction at the input bound the scan really sends' (:463) and '... for grading ...' (:467). Separately, run.ts:74 states 'the floor for extraction is 2,478 input tokens'; the measured floor is 2,978.
findings.repro: Unit level (packages/ai/src/run-truncation.test.ts style): `const {client, requests} = recordingClient([truncated(4_000), okResult]); await runStage({...common, client, estimatedInputTokens: 13_649});` then `expect(requests).toHaveLength(2)` — it is 1, and the result is OUTPUT_TRUNCATED. 13,649 is exactly `inputTokenUpperBound(PROMPTS.extraction, [dataEnvelope({pageNumbers:[1..7], gradeLevel:4}), ...7 image parts])`. API level: queuedScan({pages: 7}) with a scripted model whose extraction answer is `{kind:'incomplete', reason:'max_output_tokens'}`; assert the provider was called twice and that the second call's maxOutputTokens > 4000. Today it is called once and the assignment ends failed_final with SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS.
findings.user_impact: A parent photographs a 7-to-10-page worksheet (the app's own maximum). Extraction's answer is a few hundred tokens too long, and the scan is thrown away with 'too many questions' although the retry the code comments and the Bug Ledger promise was never attempted. The fix works only for 1–6 page scans, and the regression tests are written so that CI will never notice.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that nothing else rescues the larger scan: run.ts:253-283 returns OUTPUT_TRUNCATED as soon as `raised === null` (no fallback to a smaller answer, no page-splitting anywhere in scan-process.ts), and scan-process.ts:1228-1234 makes that a PermanentFailure so no job attempt retries it. I checked the two new tests at jobs-r2.review.test.ts:463 and :467 and the older cases in run-truncation.test.ts:81-153: every one of them passes `estimatedInputTokens` of 900, 5,000, 30,000 or the image-free floor — none passes a bound produced from an input containing an `input_image` part, which is what scan-process.ts:1314-1320 always sends. There is no test anywhere that drives extraction with more than one page and a truncated answer (grep for 'max_output_tokens' across apps/api/tests).
findings.suggested_fix: Two parts. (1) Make the retry reachable at the real bounds: either raise extraction's/grading's `maxCostMicros` so that 4E + 48,000 + 12*(2*maxOutputTokens) fits at E for 10 pages, or size the FIRST attempt's admission on the same arithmetic so a scan that cannot afford a retry is refused up front with a page-count message instead of dying after one billed generation, or fall back to extracting in page batches. (2) Change the two tests to build the input the caller builds — `[dataEnvelope({pageNumbers:[1..10], gradeLevel:4}), ...Array.from({length:10}, () => imagePart('image/jpeg','AAAA'))]` — and parameterise them over 1..maxPages so the assertion is 'two provider calls at every supported page count'. Also correct the 2,478 figure in run.ts:74.

findings.title: preTaxRefundCents divides by the whole Stripe Charge, so a partial refund on an invoice that also carries a proration line is scaled down and under-records the refund
findings.requirement: BILL-R4-3 / BUG-233: a refund is recorded in the same unit as `charged_amount_cents`, so net = gross − refunds is right
findings.mechanism: apps/api/src/routes/webhooks.ts:340-352 passes Stripe's Charge `amount` as `providerChargeTotalCents`, and billing-sync.ts:701-717 computes `round(refunded * charged / providerChargeTotal)`. The comment at billing-sync.ts:687-699 justifies the ratio on the premise that the only difference between the two units is US sales tax. That premise is false, and the same file says so: `subscriptionChargeCents`'s own docstring at billing-sync.ts:234-238 states that `amount_paid` 'also carries US sales tax ... and any pending proration items a mid-cycle plan change added to the renewal invoice', and the line-amount branch at billing-sync.ts:254-256 books only the subscription line. The repo's own tests establish that this invoice shape is the normal one: apps/api/tests/lead-billing-p17.review.test.ts:555-556 ('the parent added a child on 20 Sep (default proration_behavior): Stripe puts the pending proration items on the NEXT renewal invoice') and apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts:474-503 (invoice total 5199, charged 3999). For such an invoice the denominator is the whole charge while the numerator's unit is the subscription line only, so the refund is attributed proportionally across lines that are not booked as revenue at all.
findings.repro: 1) POST invoice.paid: subtotal 4999, tax 0, amount_paid 4999, lines = [{proration:true, amount:1000, period, price:'price_family_1'}, {proration:false, amount:3999, period, price:'price_family_1'}], billing_reason 'subscription_cycle'. `billing_periods.charged_amount_cents` = 3999 (already covered by billing-r2.review.test.ts:474). 2) POST charge.refunded for that invoice with `amount: 4999`, `amount_refunded: 3999`, `refunded: false` — the owner returned the $39.99 subscription and kept the $10 proration. Expected `refunded_cents` 3999 (the whole subscription amount came back; net 0 for the period). Actual: preTaxRefundCents(3999, 4999, 3999) = min(3999, round(3999*3999/4999)) = 3200, so `refunded_cents` = 3200 and the revenue view reports 799 cents of net subscription revenue kept. Before this diff the same case recorded 3999, exactly right.
findings.user_impact: The owner's revenue page overstates net revenue by the proration share of every partial refund on an invoice that also carried a mid-cycle proration or add-on line — $7.99 in the example above — and the support case detail shows a smaller refund than the family actually received. The pre-change code was exact in this case, so the hardening introduced the error.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the three short-circuits in preTaxRefundCents (billing-sync.ts:706-713): `providerChargeTotalCents <= chargedCents` does not fire (4999 > 3999), `refundedCents >= providerChargeTotalCents` does not fire (3999 < 4999), and the total is a safe integer — so the ratio really is applied. I checked the SQL at billing-sync.ts:806-816: for `partial_refund` it writes `least(charged_amount_cents, greatest(refunded_cents, inCharge))`, so nothing later restores the lost 799. I checked planAdjustment (packages/domain/src/donations/adjustments.ts:112-118): refund and partial_refund both reverse the $1 donation, so the donation is unaffected — the defect is confined to the money figures. And I checked every existing test touching prorations (apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts:474, lead-billing-p17.review.test.ts:538, webhooks.test.ts:389): none of them issues a refund, so no test covers this combination.
findings.suggested_fix: Divide by the pre-tax subscription portion of the charge, not by the whole Charge: pass the invoice's own tax (or `amount_paid − tax` together with the proration total already computed in `subscriptionChargeCents`) so the ratio is `charged / (charged + taxOnCharged)`, and leave lines that are not booked as revenue out of the denominator. Equivalently: cap first, convert only by the tax ratio `charged / (charged + tax)`, and fall back to no conversion when the invoice's line composition is not known. Add the proration+refund case to apps/api/tests/billing-r2.review.test.ts next to the BILL-R4-3 case.

findings.title: The new revenue note says a mid-cycle proration item is never revenue, but the revenue query sums every settled period including kind = 'proration'
findings.requirement: Owner-facing copy must be true; gross must be what the note says it is
findings.mechanism: ops-metrics.ts:150 now tells the owner that 'a mid-cycle proration item ... [is] never revenue'. That is true only of a proration LINE sitting on a renewal invoice, which is what BILL-R2-4 fixed (billing-sync.ts:254-256 books the subscription line only). It is not true of a standalone proration invoice: billing-sync.ts:283-290 maps `billing_reason === 'subscription_update'` to `kind: 'proration'`, webhooks.ts:313-331 records it with `recordBillingPeriod` for any `invoice.paid` regardless of billing_reason, and `subscriptionLine` (billing-sync.ts:211-218) falls back to the proration lines themselves when there is no non-proration line, so `charged_amount_cents` becomes the proration amount. loadRevenueMonths (ops-metrics.ts:188-199) then sums `charged_amount_cents` for every row `where settlement in ('settled','refunded','partially_refunded','chargeback')` with NO `kind` filter, so that proration money is in gross, in net, and in the store-fee estimate.
findings.repro: Post invoice.paid with `billing_reason: 'subscription_update'`, one line `{proration: true, amount: 1000, period, price: 'price_family_1'}`, subtotal 1000, tax 0, amount_paid 1000. A `billing_periods` row is written with kind 'proration' and charged_amount_cents 1000. findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a `kind` filter anywhere in the revenue path: `grep -n kind apps/api/src/services/ops-metrics.ts` shows kind only in the revenue_adjustments, support-case and attention code, never in loadRevenueMonths' predicate (ops-metrics.ts:196). findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict the note to what BILL-R2-4 actually established ('a proration item listed on a renewal invoice is not part of that renewal's charge') or make the query true to the note by filtering `and kind = 'subscription_period'` in loadRevenueMonths and stating the excluded kinds in REVENUE_DEFINITION.

findings.title: The dispatcher's new comment claims the trailing entitlement step 'always gets a slice'; the same file documents that every step before the ledger is unbounded in time
findings.requirement: R4-JOBS-4: the entitlement sweep is not starvable
findings.mechanism: dispatcher.ts:1315-1318 states 'It is not starvable either: the ledger stops claiming TICK_TRAILING_RESERVE_MS before the invocation limit, so this step always gets a slice (R4-JOBS-4).' The reserve at dispatcher.ts:738-742 only bounds when the LEDGER may claim; it says nothing about the twelve steps that run before it in runScheduledTick (dispatcher.ts:1228-1305). The same file's TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS docstring at dispatcher.ts:74-82 says the opposite about those steps: 'every earlier step of the tick is unbounded in time (an inactivity sweep sends up to 50 emails with a 10 s timeout each, entitlement syncs call the store), so the ledger can start late'. If those steps consume 14 of the 15 minutes, `runJobs` breaks immediately on the 10-minute claim budget (dispatcher.ts:735-736) and the entitlement step at dispatcher.ts:1319-1321 starts at minute 14 with under a minute left — starved by the steps in front of it, not by the ledger.
findings.repro: No production repro is needed: this is a false claim in a comment, provable by reading dispatcher.ts:74-82 against dispatcher.ts:1315-1318. A test that made it concrete would wrap one pre-ledger step (e.g. the inactivity sweep) so that it consumes 14 minutes of the test clock and assert the entitlement step still has 2 minutes — it does not.
findings.user_impact: A later reader trusts that the sweep is guaranteed time and stops looking when `entitlementsReconciled` is 0 on a tick with a long inactivity sweep — the same class of bug (a family whose subscription lapsed without a webhook keeps paid AI) that R4-JOBS-4 was filed for.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked that the reserve is applied only in the claim filter (dispatcher.ts:738-742) and nowhere in runScheduledTick, and that no step before the ledger has a wall-clock budget: `step()` (dispatcher.ts:1216-1226) only catches errors, purgeExpiredScans removes up to 500 objects (dispatcher.ts:828-877), and `inactivitySweep` is the one the file itself names as up to 50 x 10 s. I also confirmed the reserve does hold for the ledger itself — a scan is claimable only while elapsed <= 6 min and the 10-minute claim budget bounds every other kind — so the finding is only about the 'always' in the comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Weaken the claim to what the code guarantees: 'the ledger never claims work that would run past TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS − TICK_TRAILING_RESERVE_MS, so the ledger alone cannot starve this step; the steps before the ledger are still unbounded (see TICK_WALL_LIMIT_MS), so a very long inactivity sweep can still leave it nothing.' If a real guarantee is wanted, give the pre-ledger steps their own deadline check.
