findings.title: The 'identity column needs no sequence privilege' case runs as the one role 0870 did not revoke, so it cannot fail
findings.requirement: HR4-0860-01 / BUG-239: prove the sequence revoke did not break the append-only ledgers' insert path
findings.mechanism: supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:46 revokes sequence privileges `from anon, authenticated, pl_child` only, and 0870:41 says so explicitly ("service_role keeps its privileges"). public.points_ledger_id_seq was created with the identity column at supabase/migrations/0400_rewards.sql:66, under the shim's `alter default privileges in schema public grant all on sequences to anon, authenticated, service_role` (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:108), so service_role still holds USAGE, SELECT and UPDATE on it. The case at supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:998-1015 does its insert through `db.asService`, which is `set local role service_role` (supabase/tests/harness.ts:143 run()/asService). The insert therefore succeeds whether or not an identity column consults the sequence ACL, so the assertion cannot distinguish the property its name states. Nothing else covers it: the sibling case at :942 only asserts `permission denied` for setval, :982 is a catalog query, the audit append at :972 goes through public.request_deletion which is SECURITY DEFINER (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:106 area) and so runs as the function owner, and the ai_usage_events insert at :362 runs on the superuser db.sql connection.
findings.repro: In a scratch database, apply all migrations and then additionally run `revoke usage, select, update on sequence public.points_ledger_id_seq from service_role`. Re-run supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts -t 'the ledger insert path is untouched'. Under the test's own premise the insert must still succeed; if instead it fails, the premise was wrong all along — either way the unmodified test passes, i.e. no mutation of the property under test turns it red.
findings.user_impact: Nobody is harmed today, because every real ledger append runs as service_role or inside a SECURITY DEFINER function. But the check the round recorded as proof that the revoke left the append path alone proves nothing, so a future append path that runs without sequence privileges (a SECURITY INVOKER helper, or a `serial` column reached by a parent statement) can be broken by this revoke with CI green; the first symptom a family meets is an action failing with 'permission denied for sequence'.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Checked (a) supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:46 names only anon, authenticated, pl_child, and 0870:41 states service_role is kept deliberately; (b) supabase/tests/harness.ts:143 asService sets role service_role, which retains the shim-granted sequence ACL; (c) neither of the other two new cases (hardening_r2_db.test.ts:942, :982) exercises an insert; (d) a repo-wide grep for nextval/currval/setval/_id_seq outside 0640, 0870 and this file returns only comments, so there is no other test that inserts into an identity table as a role stripped of sequence privileges. No comment in 0870 or the Bug_Ledger entry for BUG-239 defers this.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the case something to prove: inside try/finally, `revoke usage, select, update on sequence public.points_ledger_id_seq from service_role`, do the insert as service, then restore the grant (the same pattern core_identity.test.ts:207-223 now uses for a column grant). Otherwise rename it to what it actually checks ('the ledger insert path still works after the revoke') so no reader takes it as evidence for the USAGE argument at 0870:38-43.

findings.title: The 'every sequence in public belongs to an identity column' guard drops any sequence that belongs to no column
findings.requirement: HR4-0860-01: the migration's stated precondition that no client insert needs USAGE on a public sequence (supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:38-43)
findings.mechanism: The query at supabase/tests/hardening_r2_db.test.ts:986-993 inner-joins pg_depend rows where the sequence is the dependent object and both `d.classid` and `d.refclassid` are pg_class — i.e. only the column-ownership dependency. A sequence made with `create sequence public.x` and then used through a column default has no pg_class->pg_class dependency at all (the default's dependency is recorded with classid = pg_attrdef), so the join discards it and the sequence never appears in `rows`. The assertion `rows.filter(r => r.deptype !== 'i')` therefore proves only 'every column-owned sequence is identity-owned', while the migration's safety argument at 0870:38-43 is the stronger 'Every sequence in public belongs to a generated always as identity column ... so no insert of any role needs USAGE here'. `expect(rows.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` does not close the gap, because the four existing identity sequences keep the count above zero forever.
findings.repro: Add a scratch migration after 0870 containing `create sequence public.widget_seq;` and `alter table public.child_subjects add column sort_order integer default nextval('public.widget_seq');`. hardening_r2_db.test.ts:982 stays green (still 4 rows, all deptype 'i'), schema_invariants.test.ts:113 stays green (the new sequence's relacl holds only the owner and service_role after 0870:49), yet `db.asParent(owner, tx => tx`insert into public.child_subjects (family_id, child_id, subject_key, display_name) values (...)`)` now fails with 'permission denied for sequence widget_seq'.
findings.user_impact: The guard the migration leans on to catch a future sequence that clients genuinely need is blind to the general case, so the blanket USAGE revoke can silently break a parent write path; the parent simply cannot save a subject, test date or study material and the suite says nothing.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I verified the case the comment names IS covered — a `serial` column records its sequence dependency with deptype 'a', which the filter catches — so the hole is specifically the standalone/unowned sequence. I also checked the only sibling guard, schema_invariants.test.ts:113, looks at ACLs and not at sequence usage, so nothing else would notice; and neither 0870 nor docs/Bug_Ledger.md:246 records this as a known deferral.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert over the sequences, not over the dependency join: select every `relkind = 'S'` in public with a LEFT JOIN to the pg_class->pg_class dependency and require each row's deptype to be exactly 'i' (a standalone sequence then yields deptype null and fails), keeping the existing non-empty check.

findings.title: The new sequence-ACL invariants cannot see a grant to PUBLIC, unlike the table cases they were modelled on
findings.requirement: HR4-0860-01: 'no client role holds a privilege on a sequence in public' (the CI guard 0870:47-49 names as its safety net)
findings.mechanism: The query at supabase/tests/schema_invariants.test.ts:122-127 filters with `pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) in ('anon','authenticated','pl_child')`. aclexplode reports a PUBLIC grant with grantee = 0, and pg_get_userbyid(0) returns 'unknown (OID=0)', so an aclitem of the form `=rwU/postgres` is filtered out and the invariant passes while `authenticated` holds UPDATE on the sequence through PUBLIC — which is all setval() needs, the exact hole HR4-0860-01 exists to close. The companion default-privileges case at :133-139 has the same blind spot: `/^(anon|authenticated|pl_child)=/` never matches the bare `=rwU/postgres` form a PUBLIC default privilege takes. The migration matches: supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:46 and :49 revoke only from the three named roles, never from public. The sibling table invariant in the same file (line 88-96) deliberately does include 'PUBLIC' in its grantee list, so the two halves of one file disagree about whether PUBLIC counts as a client role.
findings.repro: Add `grant update on sequence public.audit_events_id_seq to public;` in a scratch migration after 0870. Both new cases in schema_invariants.test.ts (:113 and :131) still return [] and pass, while `db.asParent(owner, tx => tx.unsafe("select setval('public.audit_events_id_seq', 1, false)"))` now succeeds and the setval case at hardening_r2_db.test.ts:942 goes red — so the invariant that is supposed to be the standing guard is the one that misses it. Conversely `grant update on sequence public.audit_events_id_seq to authenticated` is caught, confirming the query works only for named roles.
findings.user_impact: The CI guard meant to keep the audit, consent, points and AI-cost ledgers appendable can be walked past by a grant to PUBLIC. If that ever happens, one statement as `authenticated` resets a ledger sequence and every later append fails on the primary key until an operator repairs it — which takes down create_family, 'delete my data' (spec P4), device pairing, activation and consent, and on ai_usage_events_id_seq leaves the AI spend hold holding the owner's budget to the end of the month.
findings.not_a_false_positive: No sequence in public carries a PUBLIC aclitem today — relacl comes from the shim's default privileges (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:108), which name only anon, authenticated and service_role — so this is a hole in the guard rather than a live exposure, and I am reporting it as such. I checked that the table sibling at schema_invariants.test.ts:88 does list 'PUBLIC' (information_schema renders grantee 0 as PUBLIC), that information_schema has no view covering sequence privileges so the pg_class/aclexplode form was necessary, and that neither 0870 nor docs/Bug_Ledger.md:246 records PUBLIC as a deliberate omission.
findings.suggested_fix: Render grantee 0: `case when a.grantee = 0 then 'PUBLIC' else pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) end` and include 'PUBLIC' in the IN-list, exactly as the table case at :88 does; in the default-privileges case at :137 also flag an acl string that starts with '='; and add `public` to the revoke lists at 0870:46 and 0870:49.

findings.title: The restored child_profiles insert grant is described as 0001's grant but adds the `status` column 0001 never granted
findings.requirement: HR4-0860-03 / BUG-241: pin 0860's 'second layer if a column grant is ever restored' (supabase/migrations/0860_hardening_r2_db.sql:120)
findings.mechanism: supabase/tests/core_identity.test.ts:188 states the restored grant is 'exactly the grant 0001 made and 0860 revoked', but the statement at :209-211 grants `insert (family_id, nickname, grade_level, age_band, accessibility, curriculum_notes, status)`, while supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:480 grants only the first six — `status` is not in it. With the real 0001 grant an insert that names `status` is refused by the column privilege ('permission denied for column status'), not by child_profiles_member_insert, so the assertion at :221 ('the same policy' refuses 'active') is only reachable because the fixture widened the grant beyond anything that has existed in this schema. A reader taking the comment at face value concludes that restoring 0001's grant would expose a status write which only the policy catches.
findings.repro: Run the test with `status` removed from the grant list at :209-211: the draft insert and both step-up refusals still behave the same, but `await expect(insertAs(probeSession, 'active')).rejects.toThrow(/row-level security/)` fails — the rejection is 'permission denied for column status' instead. That difference shows the sentence at :188 does not describe the grant the test actually installs.
findings.user_impact: No user-visible defect: the policy itself is sound and is genuinely exercised for the draft/step-up cases. The cost is to the record — the next person deciding whether the revoked column grant may be restored (which 0860:120 anticipates) will reason from a grant shape 0001 never had and will over-credit the policy for refusing a status the ACL would have refused first.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I diffed the two column lists directly: supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:480 vs supabase/tests/core_identity.test.ts:209-211 — `status` appears only in the test. I confirmed supabase/migrations/0860_hardening_r2_db.sql:114 revoked insert and update table-wide (which also drops matching column privileges), so no status insert grant survives anywhere in the schema, and no comment in either file notes the widening as intentional. The surrounding assertions are otherwise real: the `finally` revoke at :223 is verified at :224-228 and the later case at core_identity.test.ts:277 would fail with an RLS error rather than /permission denied/ if the grant ever leaked.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop `status` from the restored grant and assert separately that an insert naming `status` is refused by the column privilege, or keep it and say so at :188 — 'the grant 0001 made plus `status`, so that the policy's `status = 'draft'` clause, not the column ACL, is what refuses an active profile'.

sweeps_sound: The sequence revoke breaks no insert path: all four public sequences back `generated always as identity` columns (0001_core_identity.sql:402, 0200_billing.sql:241, 0400_rewards.sql:66, 0640_monetization.sql:484), whose values come from an internal NextValueExpr that skips the sequence ACL, and a repo-wide grep for nextval/currval/setval/lastval over apps/ and supabase/ finds no call at all — supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:46 is safe.

The new BEFORE DELETE guard returns `old` on its early exit (supabase/migrations/0870_hardening_r4_db.sql:79 and :82), so a non-authenticated delete proceeds; returning `new` (null on DELETE) would have silently suppressed the row instead, and it does not.

Every production delete of public.test_dates other than the guarded parent path sits inside a SECURITY DEFINER function (0620_deletion_purge.sql:190, 0710_jobs_hardening.sql:478, 0820_support_cases_purge.sql:96 — all declared `security definer` at 0620:132/0710:390/0820:8), so current_user there is the function owner and the purge and deletion worker are not blocked by the new trigger.

test_dates really is the only client DELETE in the set 0860 guards: a repo-wide grep for client DELETE grants returns only 0100_learning.sql:499, and the remaining guarded tables' client grants are insert/update only (0100_learning.sql:496-500, 0400_rewards.sql:318-319, 0810_support_cases.sql:129-132), so 0860's insert-only triggers leave no UPDATE hole beside the DELETE one 0870 closed.

Both surfaces that offer 'remove a test date' refuse under a family-scope deletion (L-037): every family-scope deletion_requests insert tombstones the family in the same transaction (0620_deletion_purge.sql:112, 0680_retention.sql:39, 0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:122 and :189), so the API's ownedChild — whose predicate matches only target_child_id, apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:204-207 — is stopped by its `f.deleted_at is null` join at :202, and app.assert_parent_child_write is stopped by app.is_family_member.

The final definition of request_deletion does populate target_child_id (0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:106), so app.assert_parent_child_write's `d.scope = 'family' or d.target_child_id = p_child` (0860_hardening_r2_db.sql) cannot miss a child-scope request, despite the older 0600_operations.sql:53 form that omitted the column.

The guard function is not client-callable even though app-schema functions are executable by default: 0001_core_identity.sql:540 grants execute on new app functions to authenticated/service_role/pl_child, and 0870:89 revokes it from public, anon, authenticated, pl_child — pinned by hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1118.

The new delete cases distinguish 'refused' from 'hidden' (L-042): each asserts a raised message and then that the row is still present (hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1037-1041 and 1052-1059), so a row merely hidden by RLS would make pgMessage undefined and the toMatch fail.

The schedule-version bump cannot fire ahead of the guard or survive a refused delete: app.bump_schedule_version_on_test_date is an AFTER insert-or-delete trigger (0650_learning_runtime.sql:78) and the guard's exception aborts the statement, and the live-child case at hardening_r2_db.test.ts:1063-1085 reads the version after the fixture insert so the +1 it asserts really comes from the delete.

The temporary column grant in core_identity is genuinely undone: PostgreSQL's table-level REVOKE also drops the matching column privileges, the test asserts the empty state at core_identity.test.ts:224-228, and the later case at core_identity.test.ts:277 ('a parent cannot insert a child directly as active') would fail with an RLS error instead of /permission denied/ if it ever leaked.

The default-privilege sequence assertion really bites: the shim grants ALL on sequences to anon and authenticated as the same role that applies migrations (supabase/tests/shim/supabase_platform_shim.sql:108 and harness.ts:107-108), so before 0870:49 the defaclacl carries an `anon=rwU` item and schema_invariants.test.ts:131 goes red; omitting pl_child from that revoke is a no-op because no default privilege was ever granted to it.

0870's impact claim about the AI spend hold is accurate, not rhetoric: when the ai_usage_events insert fails, settleSpend extends the hold with `expires_at = greatest(expires_at, nextMonth)` (apps/api/src/jobs/spend-ceiling.ts:258-268), so the hold does hold the owner's budget to the end of the UTC month and 0860's one-day pruner will not reclaim it.

These assertions actually run: CI starts a postgres:16 service and sets DATABASE_URL (.github/workflows/ci.yml:19-32) and `pnpm check` runs `pnpm test`, which includes the @pencillift/db project, so the DB suite is not a locally-only gate.

The guard's error strings never reach a parent's screen, so their 'nothing new can be added' wording on a DELETE is not user-facing copy: neither apps/web/src nor apps/mobile/src makes a direct PostgREST data call (no `.from(` anywhere), and the API's own delete route now runs as the service role (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:836-843).
D-database.notes: I stayed read-only: I did not run the test suite, start a local Postgres or apply a migration, so every finding is argued from the code and the catalog semantics rather than from an observed failure. Three consequences. (1) I could not empirically confirm that PostgreSQL's table-level REVOKE also drops matching column privileges, which the core_identity fixture's cleanup at core_identity.test.ts:223 depends on; I argued it from the documented behaviour plus the downstream canary at core_identity.test.ts:277, which would go red if the column grant leaked — worth one psql check if the lead wants certainty. (2) I could not confirm the exact text pg_policies renders for child_profiles_member_insert, which the new regexes at core_identity.test.ts:180-186 match; the rendering I expect (`(status = 'draft'::text)`) satisfies them and CI is recorded green at 02964f9, so I treated them as real assertions. (3) My HUNT5-D-3 repro relies on pg_get_userbyid(0) returning 'unknown (OID=0)' rather than a role name, which is standard PostgreSQL behaviour but I could not execute it here. Two things I noticed and deliberately did NOT file. First, the default privileges for new public TABLES still grant SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE to anon and authenticated (shim:107; 0860 cancelled only TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES, and schema_invariants has an allowlist invariant for pl_child writes but none for authenticated), so a future public table with a permissive `for all` policy and a forgotten revoke would be client-writable; that is pre-existing, outside this diff, and 0860's header states its scope. Second, 0870:48 repeats 0860's claim that 'a hosted default privilege set by another role is caught in CI' — in CI the shim's default privileges are created by the very role that runs the migrations, so the revoke amends the same pg_default_acl entry and the hosted two-role case cannot be reproduced there; the wording is inherited verbatim from 0860:97-100 rather than introduced here, so I left it out of the findings. Files outside my four (apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts, supabase/tests/learning_runtime.test.ts, scripts/assert-test-count.mjs) I read only far enough to check my own files' claims about them, and I did not review them."

findings.title: PIN reset reads a FAILED two-step lookup as "no two-step": the 'unavailable' refusal cannot happen with the real adapter
findings.requirement: WEBR4-05 / BUG-224 — "a failed lookup refuses the submit instead of being read as 'this account has no two-step'"; WEB-R2-08 — an owner's aal2 survives a PIN reset
findings.mechanism: PinResetPage.tsx:52-68 settles the precondition from `Promise.all([account.assuranceLevel(), account.verifiedTotpFactorId()])`, treating only a REJECTION as `{state:'unavailable'}` (lines 60-65) and every resolution as 'required' or 'not_needed' (line 59). The production adapter never rejects: apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:306-310 `assuranceLevel()` does `if (error) return null` and :322-326 `verifiedTotpFactorId()` does `if (error) return null`. auth-js 2.116.0 reports a failed `mfa.listFactors()` as `{data:null,error}` — GoTrueClient.ts:6048-6055 forwards `getUser()`'s error, and `_getUser`'s catch (GoTrueClient.ts:3272-3281) returns `{data:{user:null},error}` for every AuthError including AuthRetryableFetchError (offline / captive portal / auth outage) — so it never throws. An offline lookup therefore resolves `[null, null]`, line 59 maps that to `{state:'not_needed'}`, and the submit at lines 96-105 goes on to `signInWithPassword` and `setStep('pin')`. The `{state:'unavailable'}` value (line 64) and the user-facing refusal message (lines 99-103) are unreachable through the Supabase adapter. Worse, the wrong answer is a RESOLVED promise, so `inFlight` (line 54) keeps it — `inFlight.current = null` only runs in the rejection handler (line 63) — and every later submit on that page reuses it, so the retry the comment at lines 61-62 promises never re-checks anything.
findings.repro: Create the adapter over a fake client whose `auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()` resolves `{data:{currentLevel:'aal2'},error:null}` and whose `auth.mfa.listFactors()` resolves `{data:null,error:{message:'Failed to fetch'}}` (exactly what auth-js returns when offline). Render PinResetPage with it, type the password, press "Confirm it's you" → the page goes straight to "Choose a new parent PIN"; no authenticator code is asked for and no refusal is shown. Equivalently at the page level: PinResetPage.race.test.tsx with `assuranceLevel: () => Promise.resolve('aal2')` and `verifiedTotpFactorId: () => Promise.resolve(null)` reaches the PIN step — the return shape of a failed lookup is byte-identical to "this account has no factor".
findings.user_impact: An owner with two-step verification who resets their parent PIN while the network hiccups (or while the auth service is degraded) is silently dropped to an aal1 session: the PIN reset succeeds, no authenticator code is asked for, and every /admin page then refuses with "Owner administration requires an MFA session" until they find /admin/mfa and re-verify. That is the precise loss WEB-R2-08 exists to prevent and that BUG-224/WEBR4-05 claims to have closed, and the page comment at lines 22-27 states it is closed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: The only test of this branch, apps/web/src/pages/app/PinResetPage.race.test.tsx:102-119, injects `verifiedTotpFactorId: () => Promise.reject(...)` — a fixture that bypasses the adapter's own error handling, so it proves the branch only for an adapter shape that does not exist in production; race.test.tsx:121-137 is built on rejections too. Nothing converts the null into a refusal anywhere: supabase-auth.ts:306-310 and :322-326 both `return null`, and apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:31/34 type the two calls as `Promise<'aal1'|'aal2'|null>` / `Promise<string|null>` with no error channel, so a caller cannot tell a failure from an answer. docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-224 records only the missing await and the `if (false as boolean)` guard — no deferral for the swallowed error — and L-016 in docs/Lessons_Learned.md says the opposite (an empty answer from a failed provider is destructive).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the failure distinguishable at the adapter, then keep the page's 'unavailable' branch: e.g. add `twoStepState(): Promise<'required'|'none'|'unknown'>` to the Supabase adapter that inspects both `{error}` values (and have PinResetPage refuse on 'unknown'), or return a result object instead of null from `assuranceLevel()`/`verifiedTotpFactorId()`. If those two are changed to reject, check apps/web/src/pages/admin/MfaPage.tsx:24 as well, which reads the same pair and would otherwise offer a fresh enrollment when a factor already exists. A null must never be spendable as "no factor".

findings.title: A refused sign-out that cleared this browser leaves the family's screen and a "Signed in as…" line up, and tells the parent to retry something that can no longer reach the server
findings.requirement: WEB-R2-01 / BUG-219 — the portal's sign-out must not leave the family's data readable to the next person at a shared computer; user-facing copy must be true
findings.mechanism: On the one refusal path BUG-219 describes, the real adapter clears this origin's session before reporting (supabase-auth.ts:356-359 → forgetStoredSession). So in SignOutControl `open` is false (line 69; `auth.currentSession()` → `auth.getSession()` re-reads storage on every call, auth-js GoTrueClient.ts:3047) and `refused` is true (line 65), and lines 75-78 set SERVER_NOT_TOLD and return WITHOUT navigating. Nothing else moves: a bare `localStorage.removeItem` emits no SIGNED_OUT (auth-js notifies only from `_removeSession`, GoTrueClient.ts:5263-5283), so `useParentSession` (apps/web/src/lib/session.tsx:81-87) keeps its stale `signed_in` state, `RequireParent` keeps rendering, the route page above `<Outlet/>` keeps everything it had already loaded (apps/web/src/App.tsx:168-171), and SignOutControl keeps printing `Signed in as ${maskEmail(state.session.email)}` (line 96) although this browser now holds no session at all. The copy at lines 10-11 then says "Sign out again when you are back online": a second press can never tell the server, because the refresh token it would need was deleted a moment earlier — auth-js finds no access token, skips `admin.signOut` entirely and returns `{error:null}` (GoTrueClient.ts:4091-4112) — so the retry simply navigates to /sign-in and looks like it worked.
findings.repro: Render the shell at /app/children with the real adapter over a fake client that mirrors auth-js: `signOut` resolves `{error:{message:'Failed to fetch'}}` while `sb-example-auth-token` is present in localStorage and `{error:null}` when it is absent, `getSession` reading the same key. Press Sign out → the alert reads "Your sign-in was removed from this browser…", the router is still at /app/children, "Signed in as p•••@example.test" is still on screen with the page's loaded children/verdicts, while `localStorage.getItem('sb-example-auth-token')` is already null. Press Sign out again with no network change → it navigates to /sign-in and the fake client is never asked to contact the server, so the instruction in the message cannot be carried out.
findings.user_impact: On the shared family, school or library computer this control was built for, a parent who presses Sign out is told the sign-out did not finish and is left staring at their family's page — children's names, scans, verdicts, guardian emails — with the portal still claiming they are signed in. A parent who follows the message and waits until they are "back online" leaves all of that on screen for the next person, when in fact this browser is already signed out and one more press would clear the screen immediately. The thing the message promises (telling the server) is impossible from this browser from that moment on.
findings.not_a_false_positive: App.signout.test.tsx:182-196 asserts exactly this outcome (stay on /app, show the "could not tell the server" alert) and the fixture comment at lines 68-71 states that the shell's session state is deliberately left stale and the control deliberately stays on screen — so no guard or test prevents the stale "Signed in as" line, the retained page content, or the untrue instruction, and no test presses Sign out a second time. There is no code after line 78 that re-reads the session, hides the account line, or navigates. docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-219 records the clear-and-report design only; it records no decision to keep a signed-in-looking portal after the local session is provably gone.
findings.suggested_fix: In the `refused && !open` branch, treat this browser as signed out, because it is: navigate to /sign-in (or force the shell to re-read the session so the family page is replaced) and carry the notice there, and say what actually helps — "This computer is signed out. We could not tell PencilLift's servers, so sign out on your phone, or change your password if you are worried." — instead of "Sign out again when you are back online". Keep STILL_OPEN and the stay-put behaviour for the `open === true` case, where the session really is still here.

findings.title: The ACC-WEB-AUTH-A rationale is false about the caller it names, and its test passes whether the refusal is returned or thrown
findings.requirement: ACC-WEB-AUTH-A — a refused sign-out is reported as a value and never as a rejection (apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:53-62)
findings.mechanism: App.signout.test.tsx:299-309 and apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:352-355 both state, in the present tense, that the account-closure flow "awaits this with no catch" and "must not grow one for a refused sign-out". In this very diff it grew one: apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:717-721 now wraps `await auth.signOut()` in try/catch, and its comment (lines 712-716) says the opposite of auth.ts:53-62 — "A sign-out the auth server refuses now rejects rather than reporting success (WEB-R4-AUTH-2)". Because that catch exists, the test at lines 341-362 cannot fail for the property its own docstring names: whether the adapter returns `{serverNotTold:true}` (today) or throws (the design docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-219 and the caller's comment still describe), the catch swallows it, `navigate('/account-deletion', …)` runs, and both assertions — `findByText('deletion page: closed')` and `signOut` called with `{scope:'local'}` — hold in both worlds.
findings.repro: Replace supabase-auth.ts:357-359 with the throwing contract the comments forbid — `if (error) { forgetStoredSession(storageKey); throw new Error('This session could not be ended on the server.'); }` — and run App.signout.test.tsx: 'lands on the public deletion page when supabase-js refuses the sign-out' still passes, because PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:719 catches. (The SignOutControl tests also pass in both worlds, by its own catch at lines 66-68.) A test that cannot distinguish the two contracts cannot be the guard for the one that was chosen.
findings.user_impact: No direct user impact. The cost is a contradictory record at three places a maintainer will read: supabase-auth.ts says the closure caller has no catch, PrivacyControlsPage says signOut rejects, auth.ts says it never rejects, and Bug_Ledger BUG-219 still documents the throwing version. Acting on either wrong statement — e.g. deleting SignOutControl's `?.serverNotTold` check because "the adapter throws anyway" — re-opens BUG-219, the refresh-token-left-behind bug.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I read the committed PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:710-723 and the diff hunk that added the try/catch in this same commit range, so the "no catch" claim is false about the tree as shipped. I also checked the other two production callers: SignOutControl.tsx:64-68 has its own catch and session.tsx:31 uses `.catch(() => undefined)`, so no caller at all is now catch-free, which is what the comments rely on. No `expect(...).rejects` / "does not reject" assertion exists anywhere for `signOut` (grep of App.signout.test.tsx: only `report?.serverNotTold` at line 282 and `toBeUndefined()` at line 292, both on the adapter's happy and refusal returns, neither of which fails if a future change throws from the SignOutControl/closure paths).
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one contract and make every comment match it. Keeping the value report: correct supabase-auth.ts:352-355 and App.signout.test.tsx:299-309 to say the closure flow has a catch and keeps it as belt-and-braces, fix PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:712-716's "now rejects" sentence, and refresh the BUG-219 ledger row. If the value-not-rejection rule is worth a test, assert it on the adapter directly (`await expect(adapter.signOut('local')).resolves.toEqual({ serverNotTold: true })`) rather than through a page that catches.

findings.title: /update-password decides "no current password needed" at render time, so a form filled inside the grant still saves after the grant lapses
findings.requirement: WEB-R4-AUTH-1 / BUG-242 / L-040 — the recovery grant is time-bounded and single-use, and only a live grant may set a password with no current password
findings.mechanism: `mustProve` is computed during render (lines 99-101) from `recoverySession?.recoveryActive()`, and the `AccountForm` submit closure captures that value (lines 116-129). `AccountForm` keeps its own busy/error state (apps/web/src/pages/auth/forms.tsx:18-36), so clicking the button re-renders the form, not UpdatePasswordPage. Whenever the page's last render happened inside the window and nothing re-renders it afterwards, the submit takes the `mustProve === false` path and calls `account.updatePassword(password)` with no `verifyPassword`, however long after RECOVERY_GRANT_MS (supabase-auth.ts:175, 286) the click lands; the adapter cannot refuse either, because `updatePassword` (supabase-auth.ts:250-262) just calls `auth.updateUser({ password })` on a session that keeps refreshing itself. The shipped lapse test only escapes this because it types the new password AFTER lapsing (UpdatePasswordPage.reauth.test.tsx:400-403), and typing is what re-renders the page (`setPassword`, line 170) and brings the "Current password" field back.
findings.repro: In the 'WEB-R4-AUTH-1 an abandoned mobile-link tab is not a standing grant' suite, swap the order: render the link page, type 'a-long-synthetic-pass' into "New password" while the grant is open, THEN call `lapse()`, THEN click "Save password". `updatePassword` is called with the new password and `verifyPassword` is never called, although `recoveryActive()` has returned false since before the click. Today's test (reauth.test.tsx:394-408) does the two steps in the other order and passes.
findings.user_impact: A parent who opens a phone-requested reset link on a shared computer, types the new password and walks away leaves a form that still commits the password change with no current password long after the fifteen minutes are up — the abandoned tab is still a standing grant for the one action the bound exists to limit. Narrower than BUG-242: the value saved is the one the parent typed, and any edit by the next person re-renders the page and restores the current-password requirement, so nobody else can choose the new password. But the deadline is not enforced at the moment the account is changed, which is where BUG-242 said it must be.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I looked for a submit-time re-check and there is none: `onSubmit` (lines 116-129) reads only the captured `mustProve` and never calls `recoverySession.recoveryActive()`; `AccountForm` does not re-render its parent (forms.tsx:22-36 touches only its own state); and `mustProve` also drives the rendered field list (line 149), so there is no second, later check. The lapse test at reauth.test.tsx:394-408 covers only the type-after-lapse ordering, and docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-242 records the single-source-of-truth change with no deferral for the render-time capture.

sweeps_sound: The stored-session key the adapter clears is provably the key supabase-js uses: sessionStorageKey (supabase-auth.ts:122-128) matches supabase-js 2.116.0's own default (SupabaseClient.ts:333) AND is passed explicitly to createClient (supabase-auth.ts:130-140, 188), so even a wrong derivation could not clear a stranger's key; App.signout.test.tsx:236/286 pins it.

WEB-R4-AUTH-2's premise is real, not invented: auth-js 2.116.0 `_signOut` returns `_returnResult({ error: sessionError })` before removeCurrentSession() when `_useSession` reports a non-session-missing error (GoTrueClient.ts:4087-4090), which is what an offline refresh of an expired access token produces (`_callRefreshToken` does not remove the session on a retryable fetch error).

The SERVER_NOT_TOLD branch is not dead code, and STILL_OPEN is not either: __loadSession re-reads storage on every getSession (GoTrueClient.ts:3047), so after forgetStoredSession `currentSession()` is null (→ line 75), while an adapter that throws from signOut leaves storage intact (→ line 71).

findings.title: The child edit form diffs against LIVE props, not the props it was seeded with, so it still reverts the other guardian's grade change
findings.requirement: WEBR4-03 / BUG-222 ("a diff against the props they were seeded with"); L-037-adjacent lost write
findings.mechanism: ChildrenPage.tsx:499-504 builds the PATCH body by comparing the form's own state against `child.nickname` / `child.gradeLevel` / `child.ageBand` — the CURRENT props, re-read on every render. The doc comment at ChildrenPage.tsx:472-478 (and docs/Bug_Ledger.md:229 for BUG-222) claims the diff is "against the props the form was seeded with". It is not: the form's field state is seeded once by useState (ChildrenPage.tsx:490-492) while `child` is refreshed by the page query. ChildCard is keyed by `child.id` (ChildrenPage.tsx:264 area, `data.children.map`) so it is never remounted by a reload, and `editing` is never reset (ChildrenPage.tsx:405 renders EditChildForm for as long as `editing` is true). Any sibling action — AddChildForm's onAdded, another card's activate/archive — calls `onChanged` = `query.reload` and replaces `child` under the open form. From that moment a field the parent never touched differs from the new prop, so `changes()` puts the form's STALE value into the body and the concurrent edit is overwritten: exactly the loss WEBR4-03 was filed for, now with a narrower window.
findings.repro: Render ChildrenPage with a GET /v1/family that returns Riley {gradeLevel: 3, status: 'active'} on the first call and {gradeLevel: 4} on every later call (paidSlots 1). Click "Edit Riley's details"; the grade select shows Grade 3. Now add a child in the "Add a child" form (POST /v1/children resolves) so onAdded → reload lands the grade-4 row while the edit form is still open. Change only the nickname to 'Riley R.' and press "Save Riley's details". Expected body {nickname: 'Riley R.'}; actual body {nickname: 'Riley R.', gradeLevel: 3}.
findings.user_impact: Guardian B moves the child up a grade for the new school year; guardian A, with the edit panel already open, corrects the nickname and silently puts the child back in last year's grade. Practice generation is pitched at the grade saved here, so the child gets a year of work at the wrong level and nobody is told.
findings.not_a_false_positive: The `nothingChanged` guard (ChildrenPage.tsx:504) and the empty-body early return (ChildrenPage.tsx:515) only stop a body with NO changed field; here the body genuinely differs from the server's current row, so both let it through. The contract's refine (packages/contracts/src/family.ts:120-124) only rejects an empty body. Nothing resets `editing` or re-seeds the fields when the props change — there is no useEffect in EditChildForm — and the new tests (ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:204-243) never reload the family while the form is open, so they pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot the seed once (e.g. `const [seed] = useState(child)` or a useRef set on mount) and diff against that, or remount the form when the props move (key the form on `${child.nickname}|${child.gradeLevel}|${child.ageBand}`) and tell the parent the row changed. FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:174-183 has the identical shape and should be fixed the same way.

Because migration 0600's request_deletion sets `status = 'archived'` (supabase/migrations/0600*:68), such a child is labelled ' (archived — history only)' instead, and on the planner it gets the new archived notice (LearningPlannerPage.tsx:122-130) promising "What was planned and practised stays readable" plus "Activate Riley again on the Children page while a paid slot is free" — while the purge is deleting that history and the Children page refuses to offer activation (ChildrenPage.tsx:300, ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:182) and POST /children/:id/activate answers NOT_FOUND (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:464-467). findings.repro: (a) Render LearningPlannerPage with GET /v1/family → children [{id, nickname:'Riley', gradeLevel:3, ageBand:'8-10', status:'archived', deletionPending:true}] and GET /v1/children/:id/subjects rejecting ApiRequestError('NOT_FOUND','Child not found') (what apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:195-209 does). findings.not_a_false_positive: ChildrenPage.tsx:300 and apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:139 both apply the deletionPending pre-check, so this is a per-surface gap, not a product decision. ArchivedChildCopy.test.tsx only exercises `status:'archived'` with no deletionPending (line 30), so the dead branch is untested; ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:168/192 passes `deletionPending` to the ChildrenPage schema (the full contract familyChildSchema, packages/contracts/src/family.ts:79), which is why it works there and not here. findings.title: A fresh, valid download link is shown beside "That download link expired" — the two-voice defect WEBR4-08 claims to have closed
findings.requirement: WEBR4-08 ("an expired download link speaks with one voice")
findings.mechanism: `expired` is cleared only at the top of fetchLink (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:637) and set by the expiry timer's done() (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:629-633). Nothing clears it when a new link is stored. If the parent presses "Get a new link" shortly before the old link's window ends, the old timer fires while the request is in flight (link is still non-null, so its effect is not yet cleaned up), setting expired=true and clearing the outcome; the response then sets `link` to the new signed URL. The render shows the "Download file" anchor (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:648-655) and, immediately below, the role="status" line "That download link expired for your safety. Ask for a new one to download the file." (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:657-661) at the same time. Adding setOutcome(null) to done() fixed one of the two contradicting lines and left the other.
findings.repro: In PrivacyControlsPage.download.test.tsx's harness, resolve GET /v1/exports/:id/download after a delay: get link 1, advance 55s, click "Get a new link", advance past 60s so the old timer fires, then settle the second response. Assert the exports region does not contain both a link named /download file/i and text matching /expired/i — today it contains both.
findings.user_impact: A parent is handed a working link and told in the same breath that it expired, so they abandon it and ask for another; a screen reader reads both live lines one after the other. On a slow connection the window is a few seconds wide, not milliseconds.
findings.not_a_false_positive: The effect's cleanup only clears the timer when `link` CHANGES; between the click and the response `link` is unchanged, so the old timer survives and fires. `if (!ok) setLink(null)` (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:642) covers the failure path only. The new WEBR4-08 test (PrivacyControlsPage.download.test.tsx:103-114) never has a request in flight across the expiry, so it does not see this.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear `expired` wherever a link is stored (setExpired(false) next to setLink in fetchLink's success path), or tag each request with a generation counter and ignore a timer belonging to a superseded link.

findings.title: "the page can never offer a URL that would answer with the storage service's error document" is no longer true after WEBR4-09
findings.requirement: L-038 (a server instant is not a lifetime) — the fix swapped one clock error for a smaller one but kept the absolute claim
findings.mechanism: The comment at PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:608-612 still promises that at the signing instant "the link is dropped, so the page can never offer a URL that would answer with the storage service's error document". WEBR4-09 replaced the only authoritative bound — `expiresAt`, the signature's real end — with a fixed LINK_WINDOW_MS = 60_000 (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:599) started when the response lands (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:634). The signature starts when the API calls createSignedReadUrl (apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts:49-51), so the UI keeps the link clickable for the whole round trip past its real expiry. `expiresAt` is still parsed and displayed (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:652), so the true bound is in hand and deliberately unused.
findings.repro: With fake timers, make the download responder resolve 3s after the click (as a cold Worker on mobile data would). The response's expiresAt is NOW+60s, but the timer runs to NOW+63s: assert the anchor is gone by expiresAt — today it is still rendered and clickable for ~3s afterwards, and clicking it fetches the storage service's error document.
findings.user_impact: Narrow: a parent who clicks in the last seconds of the window gets the storage provider's raw error page instead of the file or PencilLift's own "expired" line, and the code comment tells the next maintainer this cannot happen.
findings.not_a_false_positive: Nothing else bounds the anchor: the render is driven only by `link`, and `expired` is only set by this timer. The WEBR4-09 test (PrivacyControlsPage.download.test.tsx:117-125) resolves the responder instantly, so the latency term is zero there and the gap is invisible.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `Math.min(LINK_WINDOW_MS, new Date(link.expiresAt).getTime() - <the Date.now() captured when the request was SENT> )` — i.e. keep the device-clock window as the skew-proof ceiling but also honour the signature's own end measured across the same request — and soften the comment to what the code guarantees.

findings.title: The account-close sign-out guard and its comment contradict ACC-WEB-AUTH-A, and the new test asserts a rejection the adapter never produces
findings.requirement: ACC-WEB-AUTH-A / WEB-R4-AUTH-2 (a refused sign-out is reported by RETURNING SignOutRefused, never by throwing)
findings.mechanism: PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:710-723 wraps `await auth.signOut()` in try/catch and states "A sign-out the auth server refuses now rejects rather than reporting success (WEB-R4-AUTH-2)". The adapter at this same commit does the opposite: apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:342-359 returns `{ serverNotTold: true }` and its own comment says "reported by returning, not by throwing. The account-closure flow awaits this with no catch and must still reach the page"; apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:53-62 and :70-74 say the same and add that "a caller that would otherwise present a signed-out screen must read the report". So (a) the catch is unreachable for the real adapter — dead code carrying a false claim, and (b) the report is discarded on a screen that then tells the parent "this device is signed out" (ACCOUNT_CLOSE_COPY.closed/pending, packages/contracts/src/account.ts:59-61), where SignOutControl.tsx:60-79 treats exactly that report as something the parent must be told (SERVER_NOT_TOLD). The new regression test (PrivacyControlsPage.test.tsx:966-993) supplies `signOut: () => Promise.reject(...)`, a shape the contract forbids, so it exercises the fictional path and leaves the real refusal shape untested for this flow.
findings.repro: Add the honest adapter to that test: `signOut: () => Promise.resolve({ serverNotTold: true })` with POST /v1/account/close → {status:'pending', signOut:true}. The flow navigates and the page says the device is signed out; nothing tells the parent the server was never told, and the try/catch never runs. Then delete the try/catch: the honest-adapter test still passes, showing the guard protects nothing.
findings.user_impact: Small but real: on a shared computer, a parent whose close is still 'pending' (the sign-in is not closed yet) is told "this device is signed out now" although the auth service never ended the session server-side — the one case WEB-R4-AUTH-2 exists for. The larger cost is the false comment: a maintainer following it could make the adapter throw again and silently break SignOutControl's refusal reporting.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked every wrapper between the page and the adapter: session.tsx:42-53 passes `auth` through untouched, and signOutOnUnauthenticated only wraps `api`. findings.title: The in-memory refresh request id outlives the session it belonged to, and is then presented without being written to storage — re-opening BUG-244
findings.requirement: BUG-244 / AC_ACCESS_04: "one id per refresh", written to secure storage BEFORE the request goes out so an app the OS kills mid-refresh finishes that same refresh (child-session.ts:185-191, mode.ts:39-46)
findings.mechanism: `pendingRequestId` is a closure variable that only `refreshFinished()` (child-session.ts:177-180) ever nulls, and `refreshFinished()` is called on exactly two paths: a successful refresh (line 204) and a refresh refused with UNAUTHENTICATED (line 208). `forget()` (child-session.ts:150-154) does NOT null it — it only calls `unpairChildDevice`, which deletes the STORAGE copy (mode.ts:249). So a refresh that fails with a non-auth error (offline) leaves `pendingRequestId = X` in memory, and a following `logout()` (child-session.ts:278-290, whose `catch {}` at 286 swallows that very network error) deletes X from the keychain while memory keeps it. `pair()` does not reset it either — it only calls `persist()` (line 243). The next refresh of the NEW session then reaches `requestIdForThisRefresh()` with `pendingRequestId !== null`, so the `if` at line 158 is skipped entirely and the id is returned at line 173 WITHOUT the `setItem` at 168-170. Two consequences: (a) a dead session's id is sent as the new session's refresh id, and (b) the documented invariant at line 191 ("The id is written BEFORE the request goes out, so it survives the process that sent it") does not hold for that refresh — if the OS kills the app while it is in flight, the next cold start finds no stored id, mints a fresh one (line 167), and presents the old refresh token under a NEW id. The server then sees `row.used_at` set with `used_request_id !== refreshRequestId` (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:256-258) and takes the theft branch: `child_sessions.revoked_at` is stamped with `refresh_token_reuse` (child-auth.ts:297), which is precisely the harm BUG-244 closed.
findings.repro: 1) `createChildSession` over a `pairedStorage()` whose `publicApi.send` rejects with a plain `Error('network down')` and records `body.refreshRequestId`. 2) `await session.logout()` — its `accessToken()` triggers the refresh, which fails, leaving the id in memory; `forget()` then deletes `pl.child.refresh.rid`. 3) Make the mock succeed and `await session.pair({code:'ABCDEFGH', deviceLabel:'Kitchen tablet', platform:'ios'})` — this is exactly pair.tsx's "Use a different code" then "Connect" flow (apps/mobile/app/pair.tsx:71 then :55), in one app process. 4) `session.invalidateAccessToken(); await session.accessToken()`. Assert inside the mock that `storage.data.get(STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshRequestId) === body.refreshRequestId` — it is `undefined` today — and assert `ids[1] !== ids[0]`, which fails because the dead session's id is reused.
findings.user_impact: A parent troubleshooting a child's tablet does the one thing the screen offers ("Use a different code") while the connection is flaky, re-pairs, and the app is later killed by the OS in the middle of a refresh. The server reads the next attempt as a stolen token and revokes the child's session, so the tablet says it is not connected again and the parent has to mint yet another pairing code — the exact failure BUG-244 was closed to stop.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked every place the id can be cleared: `refreshFinished()` is invoked only at child-session.ts:204 and :208; `forget()` (150-154) and `persist()` (134-148) leave `pendingRequestId` alone; `unpairChildDevice` (mode.ts:244-251) can only touch storage. I checked that `requestIdForThisRefresh` writes to storage only inside the mint branch (168-170), so the early return at 173 sends an unpersisted id. I checked that no test covers a refresh failure followed by a re-pair: child-session.test.ts's offline case (229-241) stops at the failure, and all five BUG-244 cases in child-session-r2.review.test.ts (338-493) end without a second pairing. I also read the server route to confirm the mismatch is treated as theft rather than tolerated (child-auth.ts:256-258, 297).
findings.suggested_fix: Set `pendingRequestId = null` in `forget()` (and on a successful `pair()`), or make `requestIdForThisRefresh()` write the id to storage on every path, not only when it mints one — e.g. always `await deps.storage.setItem(...)` before returning.

findings.title: The BUG-244 test titled "a refusal ends the refresh, so the next one does not reuse its id" never tests that; deleting the fix line keeps it green
findings.requirement: BUG-244: "the id is only cleared when this refresh actually finished, either with tokens or with a refusal" (child-session.ts:189-190); Bug_Ledger BUG-244 lists this as one of the 5 mobile cases
findings.mechanism: The test's mock refuses the first attempt with UNAUTHENTICATED (line 392-393). In the code that takes `refreshFinished()` then `forget()` (child-session.ts:208-209), `forget()` unpairs, so `refresh()` returns at line 184 for every later call and the mock's `attempt === 2` branch (line 394, `freshTokens('access-after','rotated-after')`) is never reached — the test itself asserts `ids` has exactly one element (line 410). There is therefore NO second refresh, and nothing in the test observes the property in its title. The only observable effect of `refreshFinished()` on that path is nulling the in-memory `pendingRequestId`, because the storage key is deleted a moment later by `forget()` → `unpairChildDevice` (mode.ts:249) anyway. So removing `await refreshFinished();` from child-session.ts:208 leaves all three assertions (lines 408, 409, 410) passing. The dead mock branch at line 394 makes the file read as if the follow-up refresh were exercised.
findings.repro: Delete `await refreshFinished();` at apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:208 and run `pnpm --filter @pencillift/mobile run test`: this case stays green, and so does the rest of the suite (no other test pairs again after a refused refresh — child-session.test.ts:206-227 ends at `isPaired() === false`). A test that would go red: after the refusal, re-pair the session and force one more refresh, then assert the second refresh's id differs from the first. That test also fails on the current code, for the reason in HUNT5-G-1.
findings.user_impact: The only guard over "a refusal ends the refresh" cannot detect its own regression, which is why the id leak in HUNT5-G-1 shipped: a reviewer reading the ledger's five-case list believes the refusal path is pinned when it is not.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I traced the mock's `attempt` counter: after `forget()` the stored refresh token is gone, so `refresh()` returns at child-session.ts:184 before any send — the second branch is unreachable, and the test's own `expect(ids).toEqual([...one id...])` (line 410) confirms it. I checked the file's other BUG-244 cases: line 339-379 pins clearing on the SUCCESS path (`ids[2]` is a new id), 418-460 pins the storage copy, 462-486 the non-uuid replacement, 488-493 the unpair deletion — none exercises the refusal path's clear. I checked child-session.test.ts for a re-pair after a refusal: there is none.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the case to do what its title says — after the refusal, `pair()` again and trigger a refresh, asserting the new refresh carries a NEW id (and that the id it carries is in secure storage) — or drop the unreachable `attempt === 2` branch so the test no longer implies coverage it does not have.

findings.title: withChildTokenRetry samples the token generation before the token is resolved, so a call that triggered its own refresh loses its invalidate-and-retry
findings.requirement: child-session.ts:71-76 — "A caller that read it before making a call can tell 'the token I presented is still the current one' from 'the token has already moved on since'"; MOB-R2-02 (a refused call recovers instead of reporting the device unpaired)
findings.mechanism: `once` reads the generation at line 103, BEFORE `run()`. The bearer is resolved inside the request (packages/contracts/src/client.ts:129 `const bearer = await token()`), and that resolution can itself rotate the token: `accessToken()` (child-session.ts:218-226) calls `refresh()` whenever the cached token is missing or past `expiresAtMs - EXPIRY_SKEW_MS`, and `persist()` bumps `generation` at line 147. So a call that refreshed for itself and is then refused takes the branch at line 110 ("Another call already dropped or replaced the token this one presented") even though no other call did anything: it re-runs with the SAME, still-cached token, gets the same refusal, and surfaces it — while the `invalidateAccessToken()` at line 111 (the whole point of MOB-R2-02) never runs. The documented property at 71-76 is therefore false in one direction: a moved generation does not imply the presented token is stale.
findings.repro: With the harness in child-session-r2.review.test.ts: `const t = setup(0); await pair(t.session); t.advance(16);` so the device's own clock says the cached token is expired and the failing call refreshes inside itself; then make `dataApi` refuse every token from now on while `/v1/child/refresh` still answers (the parent tapping "Disconnect this device" in the portal between the rotation commit and the data call). `await t.childApi.get('/v1/child/me', childMeResponseSchema)` rejects with UNAUTHENTICATED after presenting the SAME access token twice (`t.server.calls` shows two `/v1/child/me` entries with one body value), and `t.session.isPaired()` is still true — the device never dropped the token the server refused.
findings.user_impact: On the one action where the child's session really has ended, the child gets a generic failure instead of the honest "Ask a grown-up to connect again", and the device keeps presenting a token it has been told is bad until the next tap.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I confirmed the bearer is fetched per request inside the client (client.ts:129) and that the client has no internal retry, so the generation sampled at line 103 genuinely predates the presentation. I checked the three HUNT4-MOB-3 cases (child-session-r2.review.test.ts:247-284): all of them pre-cache the token via `pair()` plus a backwards clock skew, so `accessToken()` never refreshes inside the failing call, and the unpaired case never bumps the generation — none of them covers this ordering. Nothing else guards it: `invalidateAccessToken` has no other caller in the app (only the wrapper and tests).
findings.suggested_fix: Sample the generation after the token is resolved (e.g. have the session expose the token together with its generation, or read the generation inside the token source for this call), so "the generation moved" means "someone else replaced what I presented" and not "I fetched my own token".

findings.title: Locking a paired tablet into the child space leaves adult screen privacy switched on, and the mode write disables the path that used to heal it
findings.requirement: MOB-R2-05 (ui.tsx:350-356) explicitly counts "screen privacy stayed on" as part of the defect when the device returns to the child space; enterChildMode (mode.ts:147) and signOutParent (mode.ts:211) both end with setScreenPrivacy(false)
findings.mechanism: `enterParentMode` turns screen privacy ON (mode.ts:181). The new child branch of `lockParentAreaOnDevice` (mode.ts:91-96) writes mode 'child' and navigates to the child home but never calls `effects.setScreenPrivacy(false)`, unlike every other route into the child space (`enterChildMode` mode.ts:147, `signOutParent` mode.ts:211). Worse, the healing path cannot correct it: `useChildModeOnFocus` (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:357-370) only calls `enterChildMode` when `mode === 'parent'`, and the lock has already written 'child' at mode.ts:92 — so when the child home mounts, the hook returns early and privacy stays enabled for the whole child session. The same happens on every app backgrounding in parent mode, via app-session.ts:86.
findings.repro: mode-r2.review.test.ts, the MOB-R4-LOCK-01 describe: after `await lockParentAreaOnDevice(storage, fx)` on a storage that holds `childRefreshToken`, assert `fx.calls).toContain('privacy:false')` — it is absent, while the same assertion passes for `enterChildMode` and `signOutParent` (see mode-r2.review.test.ts:346). findings.not_a_false_positive: I read all three exits into the child space: mode.ts:140-148 and mode.ts:195-212 both call setScreenPrivacy(false); the lock's child branch (91-96) does not. I checked useChildModeOnFocus (ui.tsx:361-364) — its `mode !== 'parent'` guard means the mode write at mode.ts:92 pre-empts it, so nothing else clears privacy. I checked the three new MOB-R4-LOCK-01 tests (mode-r2.review.test.ts:167-224): they assert clear/relock/reset-nav/mode only, never the privacy effect, so no existing test covers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `await effects.setScreenPrivacy(false)` in the paired branch of `lockParentAreaOnDevice` (or reuse `enterChildMode` there), leaving the parent-only branch as it is.

findings.title: The MOB-R4-LOCK-04 comment claims the fix stops a mounted parent screen keeping the previous parent's data; nothing in the fix does that
findings.requirement: The comment at app-session.ts:63-67 (and docs/Bug_Ledger.md:225, which states that useParentAccess "also re-checks on parentAuth.watch … so a screen already mounted as 'ready' is re-gated at the moment the session changes")
findings.mechanism: The `!signedIn` branch (app-session.ts:62-72) adds `forgetParentUnlock()` and keeps `clearAdultCaches()`. Neither removes a parent screen that is currently in view: `clearAdultCaches` only runs the two registered clearers (src/billing/revenuecat.ts:142 and app/(parent)/resources.tsx:197), so every other parent screen keeps the data it holds in component state; and `useParentAccess` re-gates only on mount, AppState 'active' and focus — it deliberately does NOT subscribe to parentAuth.watch (ui.tsx:315-321 states the reason: the account-closure confirmation). findings.repro: Mount a parent screen that has loaded data, then fire the auth watcher with `false` (app-session.test.ts already does this at line 237) without any AppState 'active' or focus event: `parentUnlockActive(NOW)` flips to false, but nothing calls the gate's `check()` and no navigation reset runs, so the screen keeps rendering. findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked what clearAdultCaches actually clears (parent-session.ts:49-57 iterates registered clearers; only revenuecat.ts:142 and resources.tsx:197 register one), so a mounted screen's own state survives. I checked every re-gate trigger in useParentAccess (ui.tsx:299-322: mount, AppState 'active', useFocusEffect) and found no parentAuth.watch subscription, with an explicit comment saying why not. I checked that the new branch does not reset navigation or write mode. The only new test (app-session.test.ts:230-242) asserts `parentUnlockActive` alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Either narrow the comment to what the fix does (close the client-side grant) and correct docs/Bug_Ledger.md:225, or make the signed-out branch drive the screen away too (e.g. `resetNavigationToUnlock()` / the full `lockParentAreaOnDevice`) — which the ui.tsx note says was avoided only for the closure-confirmation case, and can be kept that way by keeping the re-gate out of the gate hook.

sweeps_sound: BUG-244's core invariant holds for the ordinary lost-response and process-kill cases: the id is written before the request (child-session.ts:168-170) and cleared only after the rotated token is stored (child-session.ts:201-204); a stale id left by a death between persist and clear is harmless, because the server consults used_request_id only for an already-rotated token (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:256-258) and merely records it on an unused one (child-auth.ts:325).

L-007 still holds: the single-flight `inflight` at child-session.ts:222-225 is the only refresher, and every child client wraps that same module-level session (runtime.ts:34/51, homework/child-api.ts:18, app/(child)/help.tsx:36, app/(child)/rewards.tsx:50); withChildTokenRetry never refreshes on its own.

Concurrently refused calls still collapse into exactly one rotation: the generation branch at child-session.ts:110 re-runs without invalidating and joins the same `inflight`, which child-session-r2.review.test.ts:247-273 pins with two and three calls.

G-mobile-session.notes:
I stayed read-only: I ran no tests and wrote no files, so every repro above is reasoned from the code, not executed. Mutation claims (HUNT5-G-2) are derived by tracing the mock's control flow and every assertion in the file, not by running vitest.

Three things I could not settle inside my own files. (1) docs/Bug_Ledger.md:225 states that `useParentAccess` re-checks on `parentAuth.watch`; apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:315-321 says in so many words that it deliberately does not, and uses focus instead. Both files belong to other areas, so I report the mismatch only as the evidence for HUNT5-G-5 rather than as a finding of its own — whoever owns ui.tsx and the records should reconcile them. (2) expo-screen-capture's exact per-platform effect (screenshot vs recording vs casting) behind HUNT5-G-4 is from the library's documented behaviour, not from a device; the code-level divergence (no `setScreenPrivacy(false)` on that path, and `useChildModeOnFocus` unable to heal it) is what I verified. (3) I read apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts and the BUG-244 ledger entry only to judge how the server treats the ids the device sends; I did not review the server or migration 0880 as such.
