It only survives a crash or force-quit that gives the mode write no time, which I judged too thin to file.

findings.title: The new focus re-check hands a still-mounted parent screen its old state back, so the previous parent's family data stays on screen after a different parent signs in and unlocks — the exact harm MOB-R4-LOCK-04 claims to close
findings.requirement: MOB-R4-LOCK-04 / spec P3, AC_ACCESS_07 (a parent screen never shows another adult's family data)
findings.mechanism: `useParentAccess` gained a focus re-check for MOB-R4-LOCK-04 (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:324 `useFocusEffect(check)`), whose stated harm — in its own comment at ui.tsx:313-316 and again in apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:63-67 — is "an already-mounted screen in 'ready' with the previous parent's data on show". The other half of the same hunk defeats it: ui.tsx:291 `setAccess((previous) => (previous.status === 'ready' ? previous : { status: 'ready', api }))` returns the OLD state object whenever the screen is already ready. `ParentAccess.api` identity is what every parent screen keys its fetch on (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:62 `load = useCallback(() => api.get('/v1/family', …), [api])`, consumed by `useLoad` whose `run` depends on `load`, ui.tsx:486-497), so an unchanged object means no re-render and no refetch: the rows fetched under parent A stay rendered. The grant does not save it either — `forgetParentUnlock()` (app-session.ts:68) clears one module-level instant with no owner (apps/mobile/src/lib/mode.ts:55-58), so parent B's own PIN unlock re-arms `parentUnlockActive` and the re-check walks straight into line 291 and keeps A's state.
findings.repro: 1. Shared/handed-on tablet. Parent A signs in, unlocks with their PIN, opens Parent area → Children; A's cards render (access 'ready', api1). 2. A pushes a screen on top — e.g. the ErrorBox "Unlock with parent PIN" button (ui.tsx:238) or Plan/Devices/Pair — so Children blurs but stays mounted. 3. A's Supabase session ends elsewhere (portal "sign out everywhere", a password change): the watcher fires `!signedIn`, `forgetParentUnlock()` runs, but Children is blurred so no check runs and it stays 'ready' with A's data. 4. The visible top screen offers the sign-in; every hop is a replace (`SignInPrompt` → ui.tsx:453, sign-in.tsx:61 → `/(parent)/unlock`, unlock.tsx:101 → `/(parent)/home`), so Children is still in the stack underneath. 5. Parent B signs in and enters B's PIN; `parentUnlockActive` is true again. 6. B taps the native header back arrow (app/(parent)/_layout.tsx renders a Stack header): Children focuses → `useFocusEffect(check)` → mode 'parent', `parentApi()` non-null, unlock active → line 291 returns `previous` → B reads A's children (nicknames, grade levels, age bands, slot summary). A hook-level failing test: resolve to 'ready' under user-a, call `forgetParentUnlock()`, re-arm the unlock under user-b, fire focus, and assert the published state is NOT the previous object (or that `load` ran again).
findings.user_impact: On any device that has had two parents on it (a handed-on family tablet, a school loaner, a resold phone), the second parent sees the first family's children — each child's nickname, grade and age band — on the parent screen they return to, with no reload and no PIN in between. This is the privacy harm the round-4 fix was filed for, and the fix's own comment says it is closed.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked each guard that could have stopped it. (a) apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:62-72 runs only on `!signedIn` and only clears the grant plus registered caches; `parentAuth.watch` reports SIGNED_IN for the next parent (apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:142), so nothing fires for the swap itself. (b) `clearAdultCaches` iterates only registered clearers (apps/mobile/src/family/parent-session.ts:41-56) and no parent screen registers one for its `useLoad` state — the module's own doc says "anything a parent screen keeps outside component state registers a clearer here". (c) `useLoad` cannot refetch while `load`/`api` identity is unchanged (ui.tsx:486-497 + children.tsx:62). (d) `ParentAccessState` renders nothing for 'ready' (ui.tsx:413-443), so the stale content is what the parent sees. (e) The AppState 'active' re-check (ui.tsx:306-311) is not involved — the repro needs no backgrounding. (f) No test catches it: apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:196-206 asserts this exact branch and its comment asserts the opposite ("reusing it never serves another parent's data").
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the state object only while the identity behind it is unchanged: record the signed-in user id (or a parent-identity generation bumped on every `parentAuth.watch` firing, not only `!signedIn`) when a screen becomes 'ready', compare it inside `check`, and publish a fresh `{status:'ready', api}` when it differs so the screen re-fetches. That still avoids the "Loading your family" flash on an ordinary back-navigation, which is all the branch was added for. The assertion and rationale at screens-r2.review.test.ts:196-206 must change with it.

findings.title: The rewritten deletion notice promises that Privacy "cancels" a data-deletion request; no cancel exists anywhere, and the mobile Privacy screen says the opposite
findings.requirement: spec P4 / AC honesty of user-facing copy (and BUG-221 / WEBR4-02, which fixed this same sentence on the web client in this commit)
findings.mechanism: The MOB-R4-LOCK-06 rewrite at apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:236-241 ends: "Privacy shows exactly what you asked for, and cancels it if you did not mean it." There is no cancel: apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts exposes only `POST /deletion` (line 536) and `GET /deletion` (line 607); nothing in apps/, packages/ or supabase/ ever writes `deletion_requests.status = 'cancelled'`; and the mobile Privacy screen contradicts the sentence outright — "Deleting stops processing immediately and signs out the affected devices. This can't be undone." (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/privacy.tsx:381-382) — while its deletion list (privacy.tsx:430-445) is read-only text. The same commit fixed this exact claim on the web portal (apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:303-311, WEBR4-02, logged High as BUG-221) to say deletion can't be undone from the app and to link to support; the mobile copy was rewritten in the same round and carried the false promise forward.
findings.repro: Sign in as a parent, unlock, request deletion of one child's data on the Privacy screen, then open Children. The child's card reads "… Privacy shows exactly what you asked for, and cancels it if you did not mean it." Open Privacy: there is no cancel control anywhere and the screen states the deletion can't be undone. Failing test: add one line to the existing block at apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:239-245 — `expect(children).not.toMatch(/cancel/i)` — the same assertion the web suite already makes at apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.archive.test.tsx:176.
findings.user_impact: A parent who deleted the wrong child's data is told the app will undo it. They go looking for the cancel, find none, and burn the only window in which support could still have stopped the purge — the purge job is enqueued in the same transaction as the request (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:200). Every scan, result, point and reward for that child is then gone permanently.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I looked for the action the copy promises before filing. No route: apps/api/src/routes/privacy.ts has only POST/GET `/deletion`. No SQL: a grep over apps/, packages/ and supabase/ finds `'cancelled'` for a deletion only as the enum value (packages/contracts/src/privacy.ts:46) and the display label (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:321). No control: the mobile Privacy screen renders the requests as plain text (privacy.tsx:436-445). No test blocks it: the new notice test (screens-r2.review.test.ts:239-245) checks only for "Data deletion under way", the absence of "You asked for {row.nickname}" and the presence of /whole family/i, so it passes with the promise intact. And this is not an undocumented deferral: docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-221 records the identical claim as a High defect fixed on the web client in this very commit.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the web wording: processing has already stopped; the child stays listed until the deletion finishes; Privacy shows what was asked for; it can't be undone from the app; if you did not mean it, contact support — with a route to /(parent)/support. Then add `expect(children).not.toMatch(/cancel/i)` to screens-r2.review.test.ts:239.

findings.title: The notice now hedges that the deletion "may be for your whole family account" — a state this screen cannot reach — and dropped the sentence that was correct in every reachable case
findings.requirement: MOB-R4-LOCK-06 / spec P4 (a screen states what is true of the request it is describing)
findings.mechanism: The rewrite's premise (children.tsx:230-234) is that `deletionPending` cannot distinguish a per-child request from a whole-family one, so the notice must cover both. On this screen it is always per-child. The live `public.request_deletion` (supabase/migrations/0840_hardening_r1_db.sql:80-141) sets `families.deleted_at = now()` AND revokes every active membership (`update public.family_memberships set status = 'revoked' …`, lines 125-126) in the same transaction as a family-scope request. `currentFamilyId()` resolves the family only through an ACTIVE membership and otherwise throws NOT_FOUND (apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:105-117), and `r.get('/family')` calls it first (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:185) — so after a whole-family request GET /v1/family cannot answer for any adult of that family, `ChildrenContent` takes its load-error path (children.tsx:68-76 with `parentActionError(…, 'load')`, family-view.ts:166-172) and renders "Create your family in the parent portal first." instead of any child card. The API states this itself at apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:107-110: the family scope is kept in `visibleChild` "even though its tombstone normally makes it unreachable here". The web client, fixed in the same commit, still states the reachable truth ("You asked for {child.nickname}'s data to be deleted", apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:309), so the two clients now disagree about the same flag and the mobile one is the less accurate.
findings.repro: As a guardian, request deletion of ONE child's data, then open Children: the card says the request "may be for {nickname} alone or for your whole family account", although it is provably child-scope. Then, as the owner, request whole-family deletion and open Children: the screen cannot load the family at all (NOT_FOUND from `currentFamilyId`, because the membership was revoked with the tombstone), so the branch the wording was written for never renders. Failing test: with a family whose only open request has `scope: 'family'`, assert GET /v1/family answers NOT_FOUND and that the only `deletionPending` reachable on this screen is child-scope.
findings.user_impact: A parent who asked for one child's data to be deleted is told PencilLift may be deleting their whole family account and cannot say which — about the most alarming ambiguity this product can put in front of a parent — and the sentence that told them plainly what they had asked for was removed to make room for it.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked whether the family scope can reach this screen at all. (a) The live `request_deletion` revokes memberships together with the tombstone (0840:121-127, comment "The adults are released with the tombstone, not by the later purge (DB-R1-02)"), and so does the inactivity path (0840:190-192); 0840 is the last of the five `create or replace` definitions, so it is the one in force. (b) `currentFamilyId` selects `family_memberships … status = 'active'` and throws NOT_FOUND otherwise (auth.ts:105-117). (c) The screen turns that into the no-family notice, which replaces the child list entirely (children.tsx:65-76). (d) The new test (screens-r2.review.test.ts:239-245) asserts that the hedge is PRESENT, not that it is true, so it cannot catch this. (e) This is not the deferral recorded for BUG-245 — that one is only about `deletionPending` carrying no scope in the contract, not about the copy.
findings.suggested_fix: State what is true on this screen: the open request covers this child. Restore the per-child sentence (and take the web client's wording verbatim if the lead wants the two surfaces to agree). If a scope hedge is wanted for safety, put it where a family-scope flag can actually render, not on a screen that is unreachable in that state.

findings.title: A cancel that never reached the server is reported to the child as a successful stop, so the double-send and double page charge HUNT4-MOB-5 fixed returns whenever the cancel request itself fails
findings.requirement: AC_CAPTURE_06 (one job, one charge) / spec P14 child-facing copy is true
findings.mechanism: apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:279-281 feeds the decision with `await cancelScan(childApi, attemptRef.current).catch(() => 'cancelled' as const)`. `cancelScan` (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:273-289) returns 'too_late' only for `rule === 'INVALID_TRANSITION'` (line 287) and rethrows everything else (line 288), so an offline, timeout, 5xx or 429 cancel — the common case when a child taps "Stop sending" — is converted into the affirmative answer 'cancelled'. `stoppedScanOutcome` (upload.ts:313-319) then returns `{ message: 'Stopped. Your pages are still here.', keepAttempt: false }`, and scan.tsx:281 rotates `attemptRef` to a brand-new `createKey`/`finalizeKey`. If the abort raced a finalize that had already committed, the assignment stays 'queued', its `scan-usage:<id>:v1` reservation stands and its `scan_process` job runs (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1001-1013) — while the child has been told the scan stopped. "Try again" then creates a SECOND assignment under the new key, with a second reservation and a second job: exactly the "two jobs and two page-allowance charges" the fix's own docstring (upload.ts:335-345) says it prevents. The already-finalized short-circuit in `uploadScan` (upload.ts:215) cannot help, because it keys on the createKey that was just rotated away.
findings.repro: Screen-level: the finalize commits server-side, the child aborts, and `POST /v1/assignments/:id/cancel` throws `new ApiRequestError('NETWORK', 'offline', 0, 'TIMEOUT')` (the shape packages/contracts/src/client.ts produces for a fetch failure or the 20s timeout). Observed: message "Stopped. Your pages are still here." and a fresh attempt, so the next send creates a second assignment with a second `scan-usage` reservation and a second `scan_process` job. Expected: the same attempt kept and copy that does not claim the scan stopped. At the unit level there is no input for this case at all — `stoppedScanOutcome` takes only the three values `cancelScan` can RETURN, and none of them means "the cancel did not land".
findings.user_impact: A child on a flaky connection taps Stop, is told their scan stopped and their pages are still here, sends it again, and one piece of homework is checked twice: two entries in "My scans", two AI checks paid for, and two charges against the family's monthly page allowance — so the child meets "That's a lot of scanning this month!" earlier than the family paid for.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked the guards. (a) `cancelScan` has no "unknown" answer: upload.ts:287 maps only INVALID_TRANSITION and 288 rethrows, so the `.catch` at scan.tsx:280 is the only handler and it asserts success. (b) `stoppedScanOutcome` (upload.ts:313-319) has no fourth branch. (c) Neither new suite covers it: apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.test.ts:588-610 drives the three return values only, and apps/mobile/src/homework/scan-screen.test.ts:55-70 is two source regexes; nothing simulates a cancel that throws. (d) It is a real request, not a test-only path: the cancel is sent without the aborted signal (scan.tsx:280), so it runs with the default 20s timeout (packages/contracts/src/client.ts). (e) Keeping the attempt would be safe in every other case too — a create with the same key against a cancelled assignment raises `ScanStoppedError` (upload.ts:212-214), which scan.tsx:283-286 already handles — so the rotation is the unsafe default, not a necessary one. (f) docs/Bug_Ledger.md BUG-214 records a deliberate carve-out only for the `changePages` call site, not for a failed cancel.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop asserting 'cancelled' for a throw. Give `cancelScan` a fourth answer (e.g. 'unsure') for a non-INVALID_TRANSITION failure, or catch in the screen, and in that case KEEP the attempt (the same keys make the retry idempotent whatever state the server is in) and tell the child something true — "We couldn't stop that one. Check My scans to see if it went." Add an upload.test.ts case for a cancel that throws, and a scan-screen assertion that the abort path does not rotate the attempt on a thrown cancel.

findings.title: The ChildRow contract still documents canActivate/activationNote as draft-only after they were widened to archived children
findings.requirement: WEBR4-01 (an archived child can take a free slot, the way the portal offers it)
findings.mechanism: `canActivate` and `activationNote` now also cover archived children (apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:81-85), but the doc comments that define them were left as they were: line 40-42 still reads "A draft can take one of the family's unused paid slots without a new purchase (spec P11, AC_CAPACITY_03) via POST /v1/children/:id/activate" and line 44 "Why a draft can't be activated here (no unused slot), shown instead of a dead button". The helper the archived branch reuses is still called `draftActivationNote` (line 54). These comments are the only description of the fields, and the one consumer (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:258) applies no status check of its own, so a later reader who trusts the contract will add a `status === 'draft'` guard or an archived early-return at a new call site and silently take the archived offer away again.
findings.repro: Documentation defect: read apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:39-45 next to 77-85 — the interface says draft-only, the implementation says `(draft || child.status === 'archived')`.
findings.user_impact: A future change built on the stale contract re-breaks the promise the archive confirmation makes to the parent — "You can activate them again later while a paid slot is free" (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:288) — which is precisely what WEBR4-01/BUG-220 was filed for.
findings.not_a_false_positive: I checked for a correction elsewhere: nothing else in family-view.ts qualifies the two comments, no test reads them, and children.tsx:258 consumes `row.canActivate` with no status logic of its own, so the interface doc is the only guidance a new consumer has. The code change itself is correct and matches the server (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:487 clears `archived_at`), which is why only the comments are at fault.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the two doc comments to "a draft or an archived child", and either rename `draftActivationNote` or say in its comment that it serves both cases.

sweeps_sound: biometricOffer's new 'unknown' outcome neither leaks the enrolment nor destroys it: the only consumer deletes the keychain PIN solely for 'other_user' and otherwise answers `offer === 'offer'` (apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:100-104), and no time window was introduced (L-047) — apps/mobile/src/family/unlock.ts:38-43 holds.

No second child token refresher (L-007) despite two new wrappers: help.tsx:36 and rewards.tsx:50 wrap the SAME `childSession` singleton created once at apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:34, and `withChildTokenRetry` touches only `invalidateAccessToken`/`accessTokenGeneration` — the rotation stays behind the single-flight `inflight` at apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:222.

Two wrapped clients refused together still cause one rotation: the generation check retries on the newer token without dropping it (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:110), so the second call is not told the device is unpaired.

The retries added to the child help and rewards screens cannot duplicate a write: the reward ask carries a per-reward idempotency id that the retry reuses (apps/mobile/src/rewards/actions.ts:76-80), and an UNAUTHENTICATED answer means the server never processed the call.

Offering activation on an archived child matches the server: POST /v1/children/:childId/activate clears `archived_at` for any non-active profile (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:487-488) and the unique index on open slot assignments is partial (`where released_at is null`, supabase/migrations/0200_billing.sql:108-109), so re-assigning after a release is accepted.

The widened activation offer is still withheld where it must be: no slot free → note instead of a control, and a deletion-pending child gets no control at all (apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:81-85 with apps/mobile/app/(parent)/children.tsx:258).

`stoppedScanOutcome('too_late')` + keepAttempt really does make "Try again" report the existing scan instead of creating a second one: FINALIZED_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES covers every post-finalize status including extracting/checking/verifying (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:162-174) and uploadScan short-circuits on it with the retained createKey (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:215).

'too_late' is only produced for a genuinely non-cancellable scan: CANCELLABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES still includes 'queued' (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-155), so a finalize that committed but has not started processing is really cancelled and gets the honest "Stopped" copy.

The new child-home "Grown-ups" button is not a way past the PIN: it opens /(parent)/unlock, which shows the PIN field or the sign-in prompt, and Lock/Sign out stay behind a live unlock (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:213).

"Turn off biometric unlock" no longer runs on a bare tap: GatedButton calls `onPassed` only after ParentalGate passes (apps/mobile/src/family/ui.tsx:636-639), and clearing the stored PIN grants no access — the server still verifies every unlock.

The child-home test is genuinely scoped and can go red: the regex at apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:230 captures only the `not_connected` block (it stops at the first `\n  }`), so removing the Grown-ups button fails it.

The new deletion-notice wording's scope claim about the FLAG is accurate: `deletionPending` is set for `d.scope = 'family' or d.target_child_id = c.id` in GET /v1/family (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:211-215) and in the three child routes (family.ts:111-115, 140-143).

Nothing in this diff writes JSON into Postgres, touches money, compares a server instant with a device clock, or pins a fixture to a wall-clock date (L-006, L-027, L-038): the only date literal in the changed tests is the pre-existing `AT` constant used as opaque data.
H-mobile-screens.notes:
What I could not check, and two things outside my file list that bear on my findings.

Could not check by running anything: I am read-only, so nothing here was executed. The three screen-level repros (HUNT5-H-1, H-3, H-4) cannot be exercised by the repo's mobile suite at all — the vitest project cannot import react-native (stated at apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:8-10), which is why the round-4 fixes for these screens are asserted with source regexes. HUNT5-H-1 in particular is a hook-behaviour defect that the source-regex style of test cannot see, and the one test that touches it asserts the defective branch.
